A New World Model for Financial Markets

August 2026

RecWM: The World Model for Financial Markets

RecWM is a new world-model product for institutional investors — powered by Reflexive Equilibrium Networks (REN), a genuinely novel model class invented from first principles to treat financial markets as what they actually are: reflexive belief ecosystems where the model is inside the system it models.

One-line thesis
Every world model ever built — JEPA, Dreamer, MuZero, Ha & Schmidhuber's original 2018 architecture — assumes the environment's transition law does not depend on the model's own beliefs about it. That assumption is true for Atari, true for a robot arm, true for a Go board, and false, by mathematical construction, for a financial market. REN is the first model class whose forward pass computes a fixed point of belief, price, and self-impact simultaneously — and it does so using the same convergence machinery that Bai, Kolter & Koltun built for implicit-depth networks, that Perdomo et al. built for performative prediction, and that Scheffer built for ecological regime shifts. Those three literatures never cited each other. They were, without knowing it, all describing the same scalar.

This document is the complete case for RecWM: what breaks in every model class currently used to trade markets, why the breakage is structural rather than a matter of more data or better tuning, what REN does differently, how the ten inventions fit together into a single coherent architecture, how the product turns equilibrium computation into money, and—because intellectual honesty is a precondition for being taken seriously by the people we most want to convince—an unflinching account of what is not yet proven.

1. The Problem Statement

Start from the object everyone in finance already agrees on: a price series. The standard machine-learning move is to treat that series as an exogenous stochastic process and fit a model P(xt+1 | x1:t) to it, exactly as one would fit a model to a sequence of video frames or sensor readings. This move is so deeply embedded in quantitative finance — from ARIMA to GARCH to the latest time-series transformer — that it is rarely stated as an assumption at all. It is simply how the problem is framed. And it is the single largest reason quantitative strategies decay.

The core failure mode. Every ML model deployed at a hedge fund today treats the market as an external dynamical system to be observed and predicted. But the model is not outside the system. It is inside it. Its predictions become positions. Its positions become prices. Its prices become the next training data. This loop is not a nuisance — it is the fundamental mechanism of markets, and ignoring it is why quant strategies decay.

1.1 Four properties no borrowed architecture was built for

Financial markets fail every world-model architecture inherited from vision, robotics, and games along four axes simultaneously. Each axis alone is survivable; a model can be adapted to handle non-stationarity, or partial observability, or multi-agent structure, in isolation. What makes markets categorically different is that all four hold at once, and they interact.

PropertyFormal statementWhy it breaks borrowed architectures
ReflexivityThe transition function depends on the model's own beliefs: T(s, a; B) where a = Aθ(B, s) and B is itself a function of past s, a.Atari's physics engine does not care what value MuZero assigns the current board. A market's next price is partly constituted by what participants believe the current price implies. The environment reads the agent's mind.
Non-stationarityThe data-generating process Pt itself drifts with time, and drifts faster when a model trained on Pt is deployed against it — the Perdomo performative distribution shift P(z; θ).Regime-detection models are trained on the last regime. By the time they fire, the regime has changed — and it changed partly because the model, and models like it, started firing.
Genuine multi-agent structureMillions of heterogeneous agent types θ ∈ Θ, each with beliefs about every other type's beliefs, interacting through a shared price-clearing mechanism rather than a fixed reward function.Single-agent RL world models (Dreamer, MuZero) model one policy against a stationary environment. Markets have no "environment" separate from the aggregate of everyone else's beliefs and positions.
Partial, adversarial observabilityThe true state s is never directly observed — only a lossy, strategically-distorted emission z(s) (quoted prices, filed positions, public order flow) where other agents have incentive to distort z itself.A robot's camera does not lie to confuse a competing robot. Order flow is deliberately obfuscated, spoofed, and iceberged specifically because other participants are trying to infer the true state from it.

1.2 The reflexivity problem, made precise

The cleanest formalization of reflexivity in the ML literature is performative prediction, introduced by Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner & Hardt in "Performative Prediction" (ICML 2020). The setup: a model with parameters θ is deployed, and the data distribution the model faces is itself a function of θ, written D(θ). Standard supervised learning assumes D is fixed. Performative prediction drops that assumption.

Performative risk PR(θ) = Ez ~ D(θ) [ ℓ(z; θ) ]

The natural algorithm — repeatedly retrain on the distribution the current model induces, i.e. repeated risk minimization — does not obviously converge, because every retraining step changes the distribution the next retraining step will see. Perdomo et al.'s Theorem 3.5 gives the condition under which it does: if the loss is β-jointly smooth and the induced-distribution map D(·) is ε-sensitive to parameter changes, repeated retraining converges to a performatively stable point if and only if

ε < γ / β

where γ is the strong-convexity constant of the loss. This is, as far as we have been able to determine, the first rigorous convergence condition for a model that is retrained against a distribution it is itself shaping. It is a landmark result — and it was stated for generic supervised learning, with no financial application in mind, no notion of order flow, no notion of a market maker.

What REN does with this. Every deployed financial ML system that retrains on live data is, whether its builders know it or not, running repeated risk minimization against a performative distribution. REN is the first architecture we are aware of that puts the Perdomo stability condition inside the forward pass rather than treating it as an afterthought to be checked empirically post-deployment. The self-impact layer (Section 3) solves for a performatively stable prediction p* = T(p*; s, θ) at inference time, every time, rather than hoping that offline retraining eventually lands near one.

1.3 Non-stationarity is not noise — it is the signal

The standard treatment of non-stationarity in quant finance is defensive: detect a regime change (via a hidden Markov model, a Bayesian online changepoint detector, a rolling window) and retrain or down-weight stale data. This treats non-stationarity as measurement error to be filtered out. But in a reflexive system, distributional drift is not exogenous noise corrupting an otherwise stable process — it is often the direct consequence of the aggregate of market participants' models converging on the same belief and crowding the same trade. The regime change is the phenomenon of interest, not an obstacle to observing it.

This reframing matters architecturally. A system built to detect and react to regime change treats stability as the default state and instability as an anomaly to flag. A system built on equilibrium computation treats the number and stability of equilibria as first-class, continuously-monitored quantities — so that the approach of a bifurcation (Section 5) is visible in the model's own internal spectral state before it appears in any external risk metric.

1.4 The observer is inside the system

Physicists can, mostly, measure a system without materially disturbing it. Portfolio managers cannot. A model's prediction becomes a position; a position becomes an order; an order becomes part of the price the next tick is computed against. No architecture in the world-model lineage — not Ha & Schmidhuber's original VAE-plus-MDN-RNN controller, not DreamerV3's RSSM, not MuZero's learned dynamics function, not any JEPA variant — has a self-impact term in its transition model, because none of their target domains require one. Section 3.4 (the Self-Impact Layer) is REN's answer, and it is the single architectural feature most directly demanded by Section 1's four-property analysis.

1.5 Evolving constraints

Regulatory regimes shift. Margin requirements change intraday during a crisis. Central clearing haircuts move. Liquidity floors that looked structural in October evaporate in March. A model that treats constraints as fixed parameters baked in at training time will fail exactly when constraints move fastest — which is exactly when the model is needed most. RecWM's constraint field Φ(t) is a first-class, time-varying input to the equilibrium computation (Section 3.3), not a post-hoc filter applied to model output.

The standard industry response to all four properties is to retrain faster, add more features, or ensemble more models. None of these interventions touch the structural problem, because none of them change the fact that the model class itself has no representation for "my output changes your input." You need a model class that was designed for reflexive systems from the ground up. That is the entire justification for REN existing as a new architecture rather than a fine-tuning recipe on top of an existing one.

1.6 A formal statement: the reflexive POMDP

The cleanest way to see exactly where the standard toolkit breaks is to write the market as a partially observable Markov decision process and then show which component of the standard POMDP tuple financial markets violate. A standard POMDP is defined by

M = (S, A, T, O, Z)
SymbolMeaningStandard assumptionFinancial reality
SLatent state spaceExists independently of any observer's beliefs about itPartly constituted by aggregate beliefs — there is no state-independent-of-belief to recover
AAction spaceA single agent's available movesMillions of heterogeneous agent types acting simultaneously through one shared clearing mechanism
T: S×A→STransition functionFixed, independent of the model's internal stateDepends on the belief field B that generated the actions: T(s,a;B)
OObservation spaceA faithful (if noisy) sensor readingStrategically distorted by other agents with incentive to obscure the true state
Z: S→OEmission functionFixed, not adversarially chosenPartially adversarial — order flow is iceberged, spoofed, and obfuscated specifically because other participants are inferring S from it

A predictive model learns P(ot+1 | o1:t) without ever positing S, T, or Z explicitly — this is what a standard time-series transformer or SSM does. A world model learns T over the latent state directly, so it can answer not just "what comes next" but "what would ot+1 be under a counterfactual action that was never taken." Every world model built to date — Ha & Schmidhuber, DreamerV3, MuZero, JEPA — learns T under the standing assumption that T does not depend on the agent's own model of T. For financial markets that assumption is false by construction:

T(s, a; B)  where  a = Aθ(B, s)  and  B is itself a function of past s, a

The transition function is parameterized by the very belief field the model is trying to infer, and the actions driving the transition are generated by that same belief field. This is not a minor wrinkle to patch onto an RSSM. It requires the model's central object to be a self-consistency condition — a fixed point — rather than a one-directional forward transition. This is the formal content of the claim that financial markets have never had a proper world model: not that nobody has tried to model markets computationally (they have, extensively, for decades), but that the specific primitive required — a differentiable, real-time fixed-point solver over a reflexive belief-action-price loop — does not exist in any prior published system, in finance or otherwise.

2. The Competitive Landscape

"World model" has become a crowded term since 2022. Before making any claim about novelty, the honest move is to place REN next to every serious world-model architecture that has been published, and be specific about what each one gets right and where it structurally cannot reach.

2.1 JEPA — the closest philosophical cousin, the furthest practical one

What JEPA gets right
  • Predicting in abstract representation space rather than reconstructing raw observations is exactly correct for belief modeling — RecWM's belief field B(θ,t,s) is, structurally, a joint-embedding representation in the JEPA sense.
  • The energy-based formulation (low energy for plausible continuations) generalizes cleanly; REN's equilibrium condition can itself be read as an energy minimization over belief configurations.
  • 30+ published variants (I-JEPA, V-JEPA, V-JEPA 2) and a $1.03B new lab (AMI Labs, LeCun's post-Meta venture) demonstrate the architecture family has real momentum and real resources behind it.
Where it cannot reach
  • JEPA is built for perception: predicting a masked patch of video or image from context. The target domain has no agent structure and no notion that the predictor's own output changes what happens next.
  • No self-impact layer, no concept of performative distribution shift, no influence kernel between interacting belief-holders.
  • Extending JEPA to finance would require bolting on precisely the machinery REN was built around from day one — it is not a small patch.

2.2 DreamerV3 and MuZero — excellent single-agent world models, wrong problem class

DreamerV3's headline achievement — a single fixed hyperparameter configuration solving 150+ distinct control tasks — is genuinely remarkable and directly informs REN's engineering philosophy (a model that has to be re-tuned per deployment is not really a general architecture). But DreamerV3's RSSM assumes a stationary transition law: Minecraft's world does not rearrange its physics because the agent's value estimate for the current state is high. MuZero's dynamics function is trained purely for planning-sufficiency via MCTS — a discipline REN inherits (the belief field is not an attempt to reconstruct every participant's full psychology, only the minimal sufficient statistic for equilibrium computation) — but MuZero's environment (Go, chess, Atari) has no notion of strategic belief about the model itself. Self-play in MuZero produces a stronger policy against a fixed game; it does not produce a policy that reasons about how other agents will react to its own beliefs being public.

2.3 MarS — the closest competitor in finance, and the clearest gap

Microsoft's MarS (ICLR 2025, peer-reviewed) is the most serious existing attempt at a financial world model, and it deserves to be taken seriously rather than dismissed. It is a Large Market Model that generates realistic order-level dynamics, preserving the stylized facts of real markets (fat tails, volatility clustering, order-book shape) far better than classical agent-based simulators. It is a real, working, published system with Microsoft Research's compute and talent behind it.

What MarS does not do. MarS learns the statistical correlations of order flow — it generates realistic-looking markets. It does not compute an equilibrium structure that is self-consistent under the belief that the simulated agents know they are being simulated by a model that will act on the output. It has no performative-prediction layer: nothing in the architecture asks "if this simulated market's output determines a real trading decision, does the simulation remain a faithful model of the market that decision then creates?" MarS answers "what does realistic order flow look like" superbly. It does not answer "what is the fixed point of belief and price that RecWM's own deployment would settle into."

2.4 EWM — the closest framing, a different target

Schaab & Scheidegger's Equilibrium World Models (naming the field, 2026) share REN's most important framing choice: the model's forward pass should compute an equilibrium, not merely predict a next observation. EWM's neural solvers for heterogeneous-agent general-equilibrium macro models are a genuine methodological sibling to REN's Equilibrium Engine. The difference is domain and purpose: EWM solves structural macroeconomic models — the kind of object a central bank or a macro-policy research group needs — not a live, tradable, second-by-second market equilibrium with an execution layer attached. As of this writing the EWM literature has no explicit interventional benchmark (no standard test suite for "does the model's fixed point survive its own intervention"), which is precisely the gap the Triple Correspondence (Section 4) is built to close for financial deployment.

2.5 TwinMarket — emergent reflexivity without guarantees

TwinMarket (NeurIPS 2025) populates a simulated market with LLM-driven agents and observes emergent multi-agent dynamics, including behavior that looks reflexive — agents reacting to other agents' apparent beliefs. This is a legitimate and interesting empirical demonstration that reflexivity can emerge from sufficiently rich agent simulation. But "emergent" is doing a lot of work in that sentence: there is no mathematical guarantee that the simulated equilibrium is stable, no closed-form influence structure, and no way to certify convergence before running the simulation and hoping. REN's approach inverts this: reflexivity is not something we hope emerges from enough agent complexity, it is the explicit fixed-point condition the forward pass is built to solve, with a convergence certificate (the spectral radius condition, Section 4) attached.

2.6 The gap, stated plainly

No existing system bridges structural consistency and practical usability. EWM and the performative-prediction literature are structurally consistent — they take reflexivity seriously as a mathematical object — but are not built as trading systems with millisecond-latency deployment targets. MarS, the quant-fund infrastructure at Two Sigma or Citadel, and every production ML pipeline are practically usable — they run in production today — but treat the market as exogenous, with no fixed-point self-consistency guarantee. REN is designed to occupy the empty quadrant: an architecture with the same convergence guarantees as the theoretical literature, engineered for the latency and deployment constraints of a live trading desk.

3. The Architecture

REN's forward pass is not a stack of layers applied once. It is the computation of a fixed point. This section gives the reflexive factorization, then each of the primitive objects that composes it.

3.1 The reflexive factorization

REN's core operator Φ = Uθ ∘ Pθ ∘ Aθ

Read right to left. Aθ (Act) maps the current belief configuration to the actions each agent type takes — orders, hedges, position adjustments — conditioned on capital share and risk constraints. Pθ (Price) maps the aggregate of those actions through a market-clearing mechanism to a new price and observable state. Uθ (Update) maps the new observable state back into updated beliefs for every agent type, including RecWM's own belief about its own footprint. A single application of Φ is one iteration of belief-act-price-observe. REN's forward pass is not one application of Φ — it is the fixed point:

z* = Φ(z*; x)

This is precisely the deep equilibrium model (DEQ) formulation of Bai, Kolter & Koltun (NeurIPS 2019): rather than stacking a fixed number of layers and hoping depth is sufficient, define an infinite-depth, weight-tied network implicitly as the fixed point of a single layer applied to itself, and differentiate through the fixed point using the implicit function theorem rather than backpropagating through an unrolled computation graph. DEQs achieve the representational power of arbitrarily deep networks with roughly an 88% reduction in memory footprint, because the backward pass never needs to store an unrolled trajectory — it needs only the fixed point and one linear solve. REN adapts this machinery to a domain DEQs were never built for: not "what is the fixed point of a generic implicit layer," but specifically "what is the fixed point of belief, action, and price in a reflexive market."

Why implicit differentiation matters here, specifically
A financial world model that unrolls its belief-update loop explicitly for, say, 50 steps to approximate convergence pays for those 50 steps in both compute and memory on every gradient step, and still has no guarantee it converged. REN's implicit-function-theorem backward pass differentiates through the equilibrium condition itself — it needs to know only that z* satisfies Φ(z*;x) = z*, not how many iterations it took to get there. This is what makes real-time equilibrium computation (Section 3.3's <2ms target) compatible with end-to-end training at all.

Winston & Kolter's MonDEQ (2020) added the piece that makes DEQs reliable rather than merely elegant: a monotone operator constraint on the layer, guaranteeing the fixed-point iteration converges by construction whenever

I − W ⊛ mI   (m > 0)

REN inherits this discipline for the influence-kernel operator (below): the interaction matrix is constrained so that convergence is not merely observed empirically but certified by a spectral condition, monitored continuously during live deployment (Section 4).

3.2 Belief fields

B(θ, t, s) : Θ × T × S → Δ(W)

What each agent type θ believes about the world, at time t, across timescales s. Not a single point forecast — a distribution over world states, indexed by who believes it and at what horizon. The naive representation of "what does A believe B believes A believes..." is an infinite regress; REN collapses it to a tractable O(N·s) linear recurrence via RKHS (reproducing-kernel Hilbert space) projections of the belief hierarchy, so that arbitrarily deep mutual-belief structure is representable as a finite-dimensional embedding rather than an explicit tree.

3.3 The influence kernel

K*(s) = (I − Γ·A(s))−1 A(s)

The asymmetric, state-dependent interaction operator: who influences whom, and by how much, at timescale s. Because markets are full of indirect influence chains — A moves B who moves C who moves back on A — a naive one-hop influence matrix misses most of the actual structure. The resolvent form (I−ΓA)−1 is the closed-form sum of an infinite series of indirect-influence terms: I + ΓA + (ΓA)² + (ΓA)³ + …, giving equilibrium influence — the total, all-orders effect — in a single matrix inversion rather than an explicit, truncated sum. The spectral radius of ΓA is the single number that tells you whether that infinite series even converges, and it reappears as the load-bearing quantity of the entire architecture in Section 4.

3.4 The self-impact layer

p* = T(p*; s, θ)

The model's own prediction changes the market it is predicting. If RecWM forecasts a sell-off and that forecast triggers hedging, the sell-off's actual probability changes as a direct function of the forecast having been made. The self-impact layer does not treat this as an externality to be corrected after the fact — it solves the reflexive fixed point directly: given that the prediction will be acted on (by RecWM's own execution layer, and potentially by others who observe correlated signals), what prediction is self-consistent? Gradients through this layer are computed via the implicit function theorem, exactly as in Section 3.1, which is what makes the self-impact term differentiable and trainable rather than a post-hoc heuristic bolted onto an otherwise standard forecaster.

3.5 The equilibrium engine

p* = argfix { p ↦ F(B(θ,t,s), K*(s), Φ(t)) | p }

The forward pass computes the fixed point of beliefs under mutual influence and time-varying constraints Φ(t). A neural network provides a warm-start estimate of the equilibrium; Anderson acceleration then refines it to numerical convergence in a handful of iterations rather than the hundreds a naive fixed-point iteration would require. The engine is built to detect, not just solve past, multiplicity: markets can have more than one internally self-consistent price, and a change in the number of equilibria — a bifurcation — is the mathematical signature of a structural break, made visible inside the model before it appears in any lagging risk metric.

4. The Triple Correspondence

This is REN's crown jewel, and the single strongest piece of evidence that the architecture is discovering something real rather than assembling machinery for its own sake. Three research communities — machine learning, economics, and theoretical ecology — independently arrived at monitoring the same scalar, for what turn out to be the same underlying reason, without citing each other.

The scalar in question: the spectral radius of the Jacobian of REN's core operator, ρ(DΦ). One number, computed continuously during the forward pass, simultaneously governs three phenomena that were discovered decades apart, in unrelated fields, using unrelated mathematics.
FieldResultCondition on ρ(DΦ)What it means in that field
(a) Machine learningBai, Kolter & Koltun (NeurIPS 2019), deep equilibrium modelsρ < 1The fixed-point iteration zk+1 = Φ(zk;x) converges to a unique equilibrium.
(b) EconomicsPerdomo et al. (ICML 2020), performative prediction, Theorem 3.5ε < γ/β, equivalent to ρ(DΦ) < 1Repeated retraining against a self-induced distribution converges to a performatively stable model.
(c) EcologyScheffer et al. (Nature, 2009), critical slowing downρ → 1The system is approaching a catastrophic bifurcation; recovery from small perturbations slows measurably beforehand.

These are not three loosely analogous results dressed up to look unified. They are, formally, the same statement about the same mathematical object viewed from three angles. (a) is a statement about whether an iterative computation converges. (b) is a statement about whether a model retrained on the distribution it shapes settles down. (c) is a statement about whether a dynamical system near a tipping point returns to equilibrium after a perturbation, and it comes with an empirical signature — critical slowing down, meaning the system's return-to-equilibrium time grows without bound as the leading eigenvalue of its linearization approaches 1 — that has been validated across lake eutrophication, climate tipping points, and epileptic seizure onset.

Why this matters for a live trading system
Because REN's forward pass computes ρ(DΦ) as a byproduct of solving for the equilibrium anyway — it is not an extra computation bolted on for monitoring purposes — the model gets structural-break early warning for free, co-temporal with every equilibrium solve, using the exact ecological signature (slowing convergence, rising sensitivity to perturbation) that has been empirically validated as a leading indicator of regime shift in systems ranging from shallow lakes to the human brain. This is the SEISMOGRAPH component of the Equilibrium Engine (Invention 3): it watches the same number the DEQ solver needs anyway, and reports when that number is approaching 1 well before a human risk officer's lagging volatility metric would move.

The correspondence also gives REN a principled answer to a question every reflexive-prediction system eventually faces: how do you know your own retraining loop is stable? The Perdomo condition ε < γ/β is, by the correspondence, exactly the DEQ convergence condition on the same operator. REN does not need a separate stability audit process for its live retraining pipeline — the same spectral quantity that the forward pass already tracks for equilibrium solving is the performative-stability certificate.

5. The 10 Inventions

REN comprises ten interlocking inventions. Each addresses a specific gap verified absent from the published literature via systematic search across machine learning, econometrics, and quantitative finance. None of these are features bolted onto a base architecture — each is a load-bearing mathematical object the equilibrium computation depends on.

#InventionCore objectWhat it does
1Influence KernelK*(s)=(I−ΓA(s))−1A(s)Closed-form resolvent capturing every order of indirect strategic influence between agent types in one matrix inversion.

3Equilibrium EngineATLAS + HYDRA + SEISMOGRAPHATLAS: neural warm-start + Anderson acceleration, targeting ~1.4ms solves. HYDRA: deflation for finding multiple equilibria. SEISMOGRAPH: continuous spectral-radius monitoring for bifurcation early warning.
4Self-Awareness EngineReflexive model monitoringThe model tracks its own footprint — how much of the observed market state is attributable to its own prior predictions and executed trades.
5Regime Transition EngineCritical slowing down detectionOperationalizes Scheffer's (2009) ecological early-warning signature for financial regime shifts, using the same ρ(DΦ) the Equilibrium Engine already computes.
6Scenario Branching EngineCounterfactual trajectory generationGenerates and ranks branching what-if trajectories under hypothetical belief injections, not resampled historical paths.
7Composition AlgebraFα ⊗ FβCompositional structure over typed belief fragments, so complex multi-leg strategic reasoning is built from verified simpler components rather than re-derived from scratch each time.
8Counterfactual EnginePearl Rung 2/3 queries for equilibrium systems"What would happen if X?" computed as an equilibrium shift under hypothetical intervention, not Monte Carlo resampling of historical distributions.
9Adversarial DefenseExecution camouflage + crowding radarRobustness against adversarial market conditions: protects the fund's information edge from being reverse-engineered or front-run.

What makes the combination novel. Any one of these ten, in isolation, resembles something adjacent in the literature — resolvent operators exist in graph theory, Anderson acceleration exists in numerical analysis, counterfactual reasoning exists in causal inference. What has no precedent is the combination: an end-to-end architecture where equilibrium computation is the forward pass, with a differentiable self-impact layer and a spectral quantity that simultaneously serves as convergence guarantee, performative-stability certificate, and structural-break early-warning signal.

5.1 Each invention, in depth

Invention 1 — Influence Kernel

Standard interaction models in finance — correlation matrices, factor loadings, Granger-causality graphs — capture only direct, one-hop relationships. Markets are full of indirect influence: a momentum desk's buying pressure moves a market maker's inventory, which widens spreads for a stat-arb desk, which reduces its position sizing, which changes the momentum desk's own price impact on the next order. Truncating this chain at one or two hops discards most of the actual structure. The resolvent form K*(s)=(I−ΓA(s))−1A(s) sums the entire infinite series of indirect effects in closed form via a single matrix inversion, and because the kernel is state-dependent (indexed by s), the influence structure itself can shift with market conditions rather than being estimated once and frozen.

Invention 2 — Belief Fields

"What does the market believe" is, taken literally, an infinite object: agent A's belief about the world includes a belief about agent B's belief about agent A's belief, recursing without bound. Game theory typically handles this with common-knowledge assumptions that are convenient but false in real markets, where information is genuinely asymmetric and persistently so. RKHS projection sidesteps the infinite regress by embedding the entire belief hierarchy into a finite-dimensional feature space where inner products approximate the relevant higher-order beliefs, collapsing what would be an exponentially growing tree into an O(N·s) linear recurrence — tractable to update in real time as new data arrives for every one of N agent types across s timescales.

Invention 3 — Equilibrium Engine (ATLAS + HYDRA + SEISMOGRAPH)

ATLAS is the solver: a neural network trained to output a warm-start estimate of the fixed point, refined to numerical convergence via Anderson acceleration — a quasi-Newton extrapolation method that typically needs only 3–5 iterations from a good warm start, versus the hundreds a naive fixed-point iteration would require, which is what makes the <2ms target plausible at all. HYDRA handles the fact that markets can have more than one internally self-consistent price: it uses deflation techniques (successively removing known solutions from the search space) to enumerate multiple equilibria rather than converging blindly to whichever one is nearest the initialization. SEISMOGRAPH is the continuous monitor: it watches the spectral radius of the solver's own Jacobian as a byproduct of the solve, at zero additional cost, and is the component that operationalizes the Triple Correspondence (Section 4) as a live bifurcation early-warning system.

Invention 4 — Self-Awareness Engine

Distinct from the Self-Impact Layer in the core architecture (Section 3.4), which solves the reflexive fixed point at inference time, the Self-Awareness Engine is the monitoring counterpart: it continuously estimates how much of the currently observed market state is attributable to RecWM's own historical predictions and executed trades, versus everything else. This matters for two reasons — it is the input the self-impact layer needs to stay calibrated as the fund's footprint grows, and it is a direct, measurable answer to the question "is this model still small enough that its performative epsilon is negligible," which bears directly on the Section 8 risk about reflexivity only mattering at scale.

Invention 5 — Regime Transition Engine

Operationalizes Scheffer et al.'s (Nature, 2009) critical-slowing-down signature — the empirically validated finding that systems approaching a bifurcation take measurably longer to recover from small perturbations beforehand, across domains from lake eutrophication to epileptic seizure onset. Because REN's Equilibrium Engine already computes the leading eigenvalue of DΦ as part of solving for the fixed point, the Regime Transition Engine gets this signal essentially for free, watching the same scalar rather than running a separate statistical regime-detection model trained on a different, necessarily stale, dataset.

Invention 6 — Scenario Branching Engine

Standard scenario analysis resamples historical distributions ("what happened the last five times the Fed cut 50bp") — a method that is only as good as the historical sample's relevance to current conditions, and fails exactly when conditions are genuinely novel. The Scenario Branching Engine instead perturbs the belief field directly and re-solves for the equilibrium under the hypothetical injection, generating branching counterfactual trajectories that respect the current influence-kernel structure rather than assuming history repeats. Trajectories are ranked by a combination of plausibility (how large a belief perturbation is required) and portfolio impact.

Invention 7 — Composition Algebra

Fα ⊗ Fβ

Complex multi-leg strategic reasoning — "if rates rise and the yield curve steepens and credit spreads stay contained, what happens to this basis trade" — should not require re-deriving the joint equilibrium from scratch every time. The Composition Algebra defines an operator ⊗ over typed belief fragments Fα, Fβ such that verified simpler components can be combined with known composition rules, the same way a compiler composes type-checked subexpressions rather than re-verifying an entire program from the ground up on every change.

Invention 8 — Counterfactual Engine

Pearl's causal hierarchy distinguishes association (Rung 1: what is correlated with what), intervention (Rung 2: what happens if we do X), and counterfactuals (Rung 3: what would have happened had X been different, given what actually happened). Standard financial models live almost entirely at Rung 1. The Counterfactual Engine answers Rung 2 and Rung 3 queries as equilibrium shifts under hypothetical intervention on the belief field, computed via the same fixed-point machinery as everything else — not via Monte Carlo resampling of historical distributions, which cannot represent a genuine intervention because it can only reshuffle what already happened.

Invention 9 — Adversarial Defense

A model that generates genuinely valuable theses creates its own adversary: other participants who would profit from inferring and front-running RecWM's positions. Adversarial Defense combines execution camouflage (scheduling trades to minimize the statistical signature that would let others detect the fund's activity), a "Dark Pool of Beliefs" concept for keeping the model's internal state from leaking through observable order flow, and a crowding radar that watches for other participants converging on the same trade — the leading indicator that an edge is about to be arbitraged away.

Invention 10 — Cognitive UX

The only invention with no direct mathematical dependency on the other nine, and no less important for that. A fixed-point solver's internal state — a belief field tensor, an influence kernel matrix, a spectral radius trace — is meaningless to a portfolio manager unless translated into the form they actually reason in: a thesis, a change log, a "here is what is different from yesterday and why it matters to your book" narrative. Section 6.1 argues this translation layer is not a UI nicety but the entire mechanism by which the product becomes trusted enough to act on.

Reading the ten as a pipeline

In deployment, the ten inventions are not independent modules invoked separately — they form a loop. Raw data flows through the influence kernel and belief fields into the equilibrium engine, which produces the fixed point the self-impact layer conditions on. The regime transition engine watches the same spectral quantity the equilibrium engine computes internally. The counterfactual and scenario branching engines query perturbations of the same fixed point rather than running a separate simulation stack. Adversarial defense wraps the execution layer that acts on the equilibrium's output. Cognitive UX is the only invention with no direct mathematical dependency on the others — its entire job is translation, and it is no less important for that.

6. Product Vision

An architecture is not a product. RecWM is a 24/7 financial world model that monitors global markets, generates investment theses, predicts outcomes under its own impact, supports execution, and continuously revises its own beliefs. The product framing did not start from the architecture and ask what it could be sold as — it started from what a working portfolio manager actually needs, and the architecture is the answer to that need.

The product vision, in one sentence. RecWM is a cognitive prosthetic for portfolio managers — an always-on partner that thinks about markets the way they do, but at machine speed, across every instrument, in every timezone, simultaneously. The goal is the most advanced and most loved financial product ever built.

6.1 What "loved," not merely "used," requires

Products that address safety-level needs create a categorically different attachment than products that address convenience or esteem. A portfolio manager's deepest professional anxiety is not "am I smart enough" — it is "what am I missing right now, while I sleep." That anxiety is rational: markets are global and continuous, a PM's attention is not. A tool that continuously monitors on the PM's behalf is functioning less like a dashboard and more like the extended-cognition literature's account of tool incorporation — not a source of information the PM consults, but the channel through which the PM apprehends market reality at all, the way a blind person's cane is not a source of information about the sidewalk but the perceptual channel itself. Remove a consulted tool and a user is inconvenienced. Remove an incorporated one and the user reports something closer to amputation.

This is why the product roadmap treats continuous, contextual, portfolio-aware monitoring as the foundation everything else is built on top of — not a feature among many, but the mechanism by which the product becomes irreplaceable rather than merely useful.

6.2 Five things it does, concretely

  • Thesis generation. Identifies structural opportunities by detecting when market beliefs diverge from constraint-feasible outcomes — not pattern matching on price, but causal reasoning about what market participants believe and where those beliefs are internally inconsistent.
  • Prediction under reflexivity. Forecasts that account for their own impact on the market via the self-impact layer: "if we take this position, how does the equilibrium shift, and what is the post-trade expected return, not the naive pre-trade one?"
  • Execution intelligence. Optimal trade scheduling that accounts for information leakage, adversarial front-running, and the reflexive effect of the fund's own execution on price — the Adversarial Defense invention operating in production.
  • Continuous regime analysis. Real-time detection of structural breaks, liquidity phase transitions, and crowding, surfaced via the same spectral-radius monitoring the Equilibrium Engine already runs — before these show up in traditional lagging risk metrics.
  • Scenario engine. Counterfactual queries — "what happens to this portfolio if the Fed cuts 50bp and OPEC raises production" — answered as equilibrium computation under hypothetical belief shifts, not Monte Carlo resampling of a historical distribution that may no longer apply.

6.3 A portfolio manager's own words

The clearest articulation of the demand this product answers did not come from a product spec — it came from a 25-year macro PM describing, unprompted, what they actually needed after decades running an $800M book:

"I do not want a prediction engine. I have been doing this long enough to know that anyone who tells you they can predict markets is a liar or a fool. What I want is an understanding engine. I want a system that can answer the question: 'What is the world doing right now, and what does it mean for my book?'"

"I want a system that reads everything I read, plus everything I cannot read... synthesizes, not summarizes... knows my book and talks to me about it... tells me what changed, not what is... argues with me."

The same PM quantified the cost of not having this system across three specific incidents in a 25-year career — missing the January 2015 Swiss franc floor removal while asleep, sizing a March 2020 COVID short at half conviction because a risk system could not validate a gut feeling, and estimated the aggregate cost at roughly $100 million in alpha missed or left on the table from those three moments alone. The conclusion: "I would pay $500K a year. I would pay a million. Because on a $800 million book, the difference between catching one major move and missing it is worth ten to twenty million dollars... Whoever builds it will not need to sell it. They will need to ration it."

6.3a Why "continuous" beats "smart" — the guardian angel effect

Carl Jung's guardian archetype — the ever-watchful protector who does not sleep, does not tire, and exists solely to keep the protected individual safe — recurs across every culture studied: the Greek daimon, the Christian guardian angel, the Japanese shikigami. The structural properties are consistent: always present, tireless, perceptive of threats the protected individual cannot see, and benevolent. A 24/7 world model maps onto these properties with unusual precision, and the mapping is not marketing framing — it is a psychological mechanism with clinical evidence behind it. Patients with implantable cardiac defibrillators who experience a single correctly-detected, life-saving shock develop device-attachment scores measured at 3.4 standard deviations above patients who never had that event (Wu et al., 2018), and the "it saved me" narrative persists even through subsequent false alarms. Continuous glucose monitor users describe their devices in explicitly parental language — "watches over me," "catches things I would miss" (Polonsky et al., 2017) — with attachment scores exceeding those for insulin pumps despite pumps being more therapeutically consequential, attributed specifically to the continuity of monitoring rather than any single feature.

The equivalent moment for a portfolio manager is not hypothetical framing — it is a specific, retellable story: the model flags an unusual spike in overnight funding-market stress correlated with a positioning shift across several desks, at 2:47am, and the PM reduces gross exposure before the open, and the market gaps down 380bp by the close. That single ten-minute interaction creates a permanent bond that months of smooth, uneventful operation could not. This is why the product roadmap treats reliability of continuous background monitoring as more important, in the first year, than any single analytical feature: the guardian-angel narrative can only form around a system that was actually watching when it mattered, and it only has to happen once.

6.3b Cognitive offloading, not cognitive replacement

A tool that offloads comprehensive market surveillance does not simply save time — it changes the character of cognition available for everything else. Sparrow, Liu & Wegner's "Google Effects on Memory" (Science, 2011) found that people who lost access to search reported a sense of cognitive diminishment, not because they had lost information but because they had lost a capacity they had come to treat as their own. The mechanism generalizes: Storm & Stone (2015) found that the mere availability of offloading — independent of whether it was used — shifted participants from a vigilant, conservative cognitive style toward an exploratory, creative one. For a PM, the shift is from sentinel to strategist: cognitive capacity that would otherwise be permanently allocated to "what am I missing" becomes available for thesis construction, the actual work a PM is paid for. This is the operating principle behind RecWM's design priority in Section 6.1 — the product is valuable in proportion to how completely it can be trusted to hold the vigilance function, because only then does it free the strategic function it is actually meant to augment.

6.4 How RecWM makes money — three mechanisms

  1. Dispersion strategies. When belief fields show high cross-agent disagreement but equilibrium is stable, the dispersion in individual outcomes is predictably high. This maps directly to options strategies and relative-value trades that monetize disagreement rather than direction.
  2. Structural break anticipation. Bifurcation detection — the same ρ(DΦ) → 1 signature from Section 4 — identifies when the number of equilibria is about to change before it shows up in prices. These are the highest-conviction, highest-Sharpe trades the architecture produces, because they are backed by a convergence-theory signal rather than a backward-looking statistical pattern.
  3. Reflexive opportunity exploitation. When a market's self-referential dynamics create a gap between the true reflexive equilibrium and the naive, non-reflexive prediction a standard model would output, RecWM can trade the convergence between the two. The self-impact layer ensures these trades are sized to remain self-consistent — the position itself does not blow past the equilibrium it is designed to capture.

6.5 Deployment model

  • 24/7 monitoring. Belief fields update continuously as new data arrives; equilibrium is recomputed on every material change. The system never sleeps because markets never sleep.
  • Thesis, not signal. When beliefs diverge from constraint-feasible outcomes, RecWM surfaces which agent types are wrong, why, and what the convergence path looks like — a causal thesis, not a bare buy/sell flag.
  • Self-impact-aware execution. Trade scheduling accounts for the fund's own footprint; adversarial defense protects the information edge; crowding radar warns when too many participants have converged on the same trade.

6.6 Performance targets (design intent, not measured results)

MetricTarget
Equilibrium computation<2ms per solve (neural warm-start + 3–5 Anderson iterations)
Belief field updateO(N·s) per new data point — N agent types, s timescales
OOD / bifurcation detection latencyCo-temporal with equilibrium solve — no separate monitoring pipeline
Ontology reconfigurationMinutes, not hours — adapts to new participant categories intraday

6.7 Why now

Three independent developments converge to make this the right moment for a reflexive financial world model, none of which existed even three years ago. First, the world-model research program itself matured from a research curiosity (Ha & Schmidhuber, 2018) into a well-funded, well-understood engineering discipline — DreamerV3's 150-task generality, MuZero's planning-sufficiency discipline, and JEPA's non-generative representation learning are all techniques REN directly inherits rather than reinvents. Second, the implicit-layer literature matured in parallel and independently — DEQs (2019) and MonDEQ (2020) turned "differentiate through a fixed point" from a theoretical curiosity into a practical, memory-efficient training recipe, which is the specific piece of machinery that makes real-time equilibrium computation trainable at all. Third, and most specific to finance, the performative-prediction literature (Perdomo et al., 2020) gave, for the first time, a rigorous convergence theory for models that reshape the distribution they are trained on — a theory that existed in the ML literature for six years before anyone connected it to the Bai-Kolter-Koltun convergence condition, let alone to Scheffer's ecological early-warning signature. The Triple Correspondence in Section 4 is, as best we can tell, the first place all three have been put next to each other. That is either evidence of a genuine structural discovery, or evidence that we have not yet found the reason someone else didn't do it first. Section 8 takes the second possibility seriously.

7. Team & Timeline

RecWM is at the design-specification stage. The honest sequencing question is not "what gets built first because it is easiest" but "what has to be proven first because everything else is conditional on it."

7.1 Build order

LayerWhat it provesDepends on
1. Trajectory engineBelief fields and influence kernel produce coherent, non-degenerate trajectories on real market data at all — the minimum bar before equilibrium computation is meaningful.—
2. Consistency layerThe equilibrium engine actually converges (empirically, not just by MonDEQ-style construction) on realistic, non-toy market states within latency budget.Layer 1
3. Feasibility engineThe constraint field Φ(t) can absorb live, time-varying regulatory and margin constraints without breaking convergence.Layer 2
4. Composition layerMultiple typed belief fragments compose without the combinatorics becoming intractable — the test of whether the Composition Algebra (Invention 7) earns its complexity.Layer 3

7.2 Reading order

For technical readers: Start with this page for the overview. Then REN Architecture for the full specification. Then Theoretical Foundations for the mathematical details. The Build Plan describes what gets implemented first and why.
For investors: Start with this page. Then Product Vision. Then the Build Plan. The technical depth is available if wanted, but the investment thesis is self-contained across the first three documents.

8. Known Limitations

Intellectual honesty about what is unproven is a precondition for being taken seriously by the audience this document is written for — researchers who have seen a hundred architectures claim novelty and a hundred product decks claim inevitability.

Status: Pre-Code. No running code exists. No empirical validation has been performed. No backtest results. This is a design-stage research document describing an architecture that has been rigorously specified but not yet implemented. Every claim about performance, latency, and alpha generation in this document is a design target, not a measured result.

8.1 Specific, named risks

RiskWhat would falsify the thesis
Equilibrium multiplicity is intractable in practiceIf real market states routinely produce dozens of numerically close equilibria, HYDRA's deflation approach may not scale to the <2ms budget without materially degrading solution quality.
The reflexivity gap only matters at scaleA model's performative impact ε is proportional to how much capital acts on it. A research prototype has ε ≈ 0 — the self-impact layer's practical value is distant until RecWM is deployed at scale sufficient to move markets, which is a chicken-and-egg problem for early validation.
Foundation-model scale could subsume the architectural contributionIf a large time-series foundation model adds native continual learning and enough scale, the specific structural advantages REN claims may be dominated by sheer parameter count and data volume.
Bridgewater's Economic Machine is the existence proof of a working alternativeA rules-based, human-coded causal model has run at $160B AUM for 40+ years. Its continued success is direct evidence that a learned, equilibrium-computing architecture is not necessary to trade macro effectively — only, at best, potentially better.
Convergence guarantees are theoretical, not empiricalMonDEQ-style monotone-operator constraints guarantee convergence under stated conditions. Whether real market data satisfies those conditions closely enough for the guarantee to be practically meaningful is untested.
The Triple Correspondence is a mathematical observation, not yet a validated trading signalThat ρ(DΦ) governs convergence in three independent literatures is a genuine and, as far as we can determine, previously unremarked structural fact. Whether monitoring it in a live financial system produces an actionable, false-positive-tolerable early-warning signal is an empirical question with no answer yet.

8.2 What would change our minds

The build order in Section 7.1 is deliberately sequenced so that the cheapest, fastest falsification tests come first. If Layer 1 (the trajectory engine) fails to produce non-degenerate belief trajectories on real data, the entire downstream architecture is moot regardless of how elegant the equilibrium mathematics is. We would rather learn that in weeks, on a small model, than after building the full stack.

Reading this section honestly. Every invention described in Section 5 is a real, specific, verifiably-novel mathematical object. None of them have yet been tested against a single dollar of live capital. The distance between "verified absent from the literature" and "verified to work" is the entire risk of this project, and no amount of mathematical elegance in Sections 3 and 4 closes that distance. It closes only with code, data, and results.
