A backtesting platform Backtesting asks "would this strategy have worked in the past?" RecWM asks "is this strategy consistent with the current belief equilibrium and robust to plausible perturbations?" Forward reasoning, not historical replay.
An execution algorithm TWAP/VWAP optimize for fill quality against historical microstructure. RecWM's execution layer optimizes against the reflexive impact of the trade on the equilibrium — a fundamentally different optimization target.
A single model that ships a signal RecWM is a continuously-running system with perception, reasoning, prediction, and action components. It ships theses, scenarios, and deployment recommendations — not a single alpha signal.

5.1 Elaborating Each Distinction

Not a better Bloomberg terminal. A terminal's job is to make existing, already-computed quantities visible faster and more conveniently than the alternative — it does not compute anything that was not already computable from public data by some other means. Its value is aggregation, latency, and interface. RecWM's belief field Bt, its equilibrium set {bi*}, and its bifurcation distance δbif are not quantities that exist anywhere for a terminal to display — they are the output of a fixed-point solve over a model of participant beliefs that no data vendor computes. Overlapping inputs (both read prices, filings, and flow data) do not imply overlapping outputs.

Not a chatbot that talks about markets. A large language model can produce fluent, plausible-sounding commentary about market dynamics because it has been trained on a vast corpus of humans doing exactly that — but it has no mechanism to solve Φ(b*)=b*, no representation of a belief field as a natural-parameter matrix, and no spectral monitor on a Jacobian it does not compute. It can describe reflexivity in prose; it cannot detect ρ(DΦ) crossing 1 in real time, because that requires an explicit differentiable dynamical system, not a next-token predictor over text. RecWM may use language models as an interface layer or as one input channel (parsing central bank text into the policy fragment, Section 3.2) — but its reasoning core is the equilibrium engine, not an LLM's internal weights.

Not a risk management system. A risk system's job is measurement: given a historical or parametric distribution of factor returns, compute the exposure of a portfolio to a shock of a given size along a given factor. It answers "how much would I lose if X happened," where X is specified exogenously by the risk model's user. RecWM answers a logically prior question: "is X currently a live possibility, how does its probability change as beliefs evolve, and what mechanism would produce it." A risk system with a covariance matrix estimated from 2017–2019 data would have reported LTCM-style convergence trades as low-risk, because the correlation spike that materialized in 1998 had not yet been observed; RecWM's crowding diagnostic (Section 4.4) is designed to catch exactly the condition — large mutual best-response coefficients — that produces such a spike before it appears in any historical covariance estimate.

Not a backtesting platform. Backtesting is fundamentally retrospective: it replays history and asks whether a rule would have performed well on that specific historical path. It cannot, by construction, evaluate a strategy against a scenario that never occurred, and it silently assumes the market's reflexive structure during the backtest period is representative of the structure the strategy will face live — an assumption that Section 2's four case studies show is exactly the assumption that fails at regime transitions. RecWM's structural counterfactual engine (Section 4.3) evaluates a strategy against a new equilibrium computed under an intervened state, which can represent configurations with zero historical precedent.

Not an execution algorithm. TWAP and VWAP schedules are optimized against a statistical model of intraday volume and volatility patterns estimated from historical microstructure — they treat market impact as an exogenous cost curve to be minimized, independent of what the trade itself implies about the trader's beliefs. RecWM's Self-Impact Layer (Section 4.2) treats the trade as an action inside the same fixed-point computation that produced the thesis in the first place — the execution schedule is chosen jointly with the equilibrium the trade is expected to produce, not fitted afterward to a separate cost model.

Not a single model that ships a signal. A signal is a scalar or a small vector, refreshed on a schedule, with no internal state connecting one output to the next. RecWM is a persistent system: its belief field, its tracked equilibrium landscape (the CONTINUATOR data structure, a time-indexed record of every equilibrium branch's birth, death, and stability history), and its novelty and observability scores all carry state across the loop's iterations. Its outputs are theses with attached mechanisms, scenario-conditioned portfolios, and execution plans that account for the system's own prior actions — not an isolated number regenerated from scratch each time it is queried.

6. The World-Model Loop: A Concrete Example

Tuesday, 14:32 UTC. RecWM is running continuously.

Observe. The Information Fusion layer registers, across the seven state fragments: (Risk fragment, x_R) 10Y Treasury yield jumps 8bp in 20 minutes, on volume 2.3x the trailing 20-day average for this time of day; (Momentum fragment, x_M) S&P futures drop 0.4%, and the log-signature trend-strength estimate μequity flips from +0.6 to −0.3 on a 15-minute lookback; (Risk fragment, x_R) the VIX term structure inverts at the 2-week point — the front-month implied vol rises above the 1-month, a specific, quotable signature that the model's observation function Φ(x_R, x_S, x_N) treats as directly informative about near-term tail pricing; (Structure fragment, x_S) dealer gamma exposure estimates for SPX, updated from options open interest, are recomputed at gamma_SPX ≈ −$1.4bn per 1% move — dealers are net short gamma at the current strike concentration, meaning their hedging flows will amplify, not dampen, further moves; (Momentum fragment, x_M) CTA flow models, calibrated on the observed trend-strength flip, estimate $2.1B in systematic selling over the next 2 hours; (Sentiment/Policy fragments, x_N/x_P) a Fed governor speech transcript, parsed through the text channel Xi_n(x_P, x_N), mentions "data dependent" three times — up from the recent baseline of once — nudging the hawkishness score for that governor upward.

Infer beliefs. The Belief Field updates, row by row, one row per agent type. Discretionary macro funds' implied belief about the terminal rate, encoded in the natural parameter η(θmacro), shifts up 15bp — inferred not from a survey but from the observed repricing of Fed funds futures relative to what those funds' known duration positioning implies about their reaction function. CTA beliefs are near-mechanical (trend-following rules operating directly on realized price path, already captured in the momentum fragment's own dynamics) and require no separate inference step — their action is close to a deterministic function of x_M. Market maker beliefs, inferred from the shift in their quoted bid-ask asymmetry and the dealer gamma estimate above, shift toward expecting a second wave of selling from risk-parity rebalancing at 15:00 — specifically, the interaction-matrix entry K_{marketmaker, risk-parity} in the belief hierarchy's attention structure is currently elevated, meaning market makers are weighting risk-parity behavior heavily in their own short-horizon belief formation, a state-dependent modulation of K_t triggered by the realized-vol regime. Value-oriented equity funds show no belief revision yet — their timescale is weeks, not hours, and the Influence Kernel evaluated at a slow log-timescale s_slow shows negligible propagation of this shock into their row of the belief field, versus a large propagation into the fast-timescale kernel K*(s_fast).

Compute equilibrium. ATLAS, warm-started from a neural predictor trained on similar historical configurations, finds two self-consistent equilibria in roughly 4ms combined. Equilibrium A: the selling is absorbed by market makers and value funds stepping in below current levels, implied vol normalizes over the next hour — locally stable, ρ(DΦ(b*_A)) ≈ 0.71, assigned probability 0.65 via Boltzmann weighting on stability energy. Equilibrium B: the risk-parity rebalancing at 15:00 triggers a second wave, amplified by dealers' negative gamma exposure (their hedging sells into the decline rather than buying against it), VIX spikes above 22, credit spreads widen sympathetically through the credit fragment's coupling block A_r^{CL} — also locally stable once reached, ρ(DΦ(b*_B)) ≈ 0.58, probability 0.30. HYDRA's deflation search finds a third, unstable equilibrium at the tipping point between A and B — ρ(DΦ(b*_C)) ≈ 1.4, probability 0.05 under the same weighting, consistent with the Poincaré–Hopf expectation of an odd total count (3) with the middle equilibrium unstable. SEISMOGRAPH reports the normalized bifurcation distance for equilibrium A at δ̂bif ≈ 0.12 in units that translate to roughly 6–9 minutes at the current closure rate — equilibrium A is not gone, but it is getting closer to vanishing, specifically via what the eigenvalue-crossing type classifies as an approaching fold: a real eigenvalue of DΦ(b*_A) is moving toward 1, meaning that if the closure continues, equilibrium A does not gradually weaken, it disappears outright at a specific moment.

Predict. Under equilibrium A, the portfolio is fine (expected Sharpe contribution +0.02 over the next 24h, computed by propagating the current book through the mean-variance-plus-higher-moment demand function evaluated at b*_A). Under equilibrium B, the portfolio takes a −1.8% hit from its long credit position, driven specifically through the x_R–x_C coupling block that widens spreads sympathetically with the vol spike. The probability-weighted expected outcome is modestly negative (0.65×0.02 + 0.30×(−1.8%) ≈ −0.52%), but reporting only that blended number would discard the information that actually matters: the tail risk is not diffuse, it is concentrated in one specific, identifiable, named mechanism — risk-parity rebalancing at 15:00 cascading into credit through dealers' negative gamma exposure — and that mechanism has a bifurcation countdown attached to it.

Act. RecWM generates a thesis, not a signal: "Reduce credit exposure by 30% in the next 45 minutes. The cost of this hedge is 4bp of carry. The benefit is eliminating the −1.8% tail in the bifurcation-B scenario, which has probability 0.30 and is rising as equilibrium A's bifurcation distance closes. The Self-Impact Layer, solving p* = T(p*; s, θ) with the contemplated 30% credit reduction folded into the action-selection stage alongside every other agent type's inferred action, estimates our own selling will move credit spreads by 0.5bp — negligible self-impact at this size, so the hedge does not meaningfully worsen the scenario it is meant to protect against." Note precisely what makes this different from a VaR-style hedge recommendation: the sizing, the timing (45 minutes, tied to the 15:00 rebalancing window), and the self-impact check are all read off the same equilibrium computation, not three separately bolted-on estimates.

Observe. The loop restarts at 14:33. The model now includes the consequences of its own recommended action in the next belief update: if the PM executes the hedge, RecWM's Observe stage at 14:33 registers the resulting sell flow in the credit fragment's measurement channel, updates the liquidity fragment's dealer inventory estimate accordingly, and the belief field at 14:33 is inferred including this new data point — the model's own action from the previous cycle is now part of the market state it is inferring beliefs about, exactly as the formal loop specification in Section 3.1 requires.

What no other system could have done here: (1) Inferred different beliefs for different participant types from the same market data, and localized which agent types had and had not yet updated; (2) found two genuinely self-consistent equilibria, plus the unstable equilibrium between them, rather than one "expected" outcome or a single confidence interval; (3) quantified the probability of a regime transition via a bifurcation distance with time units, not a qualitative "elevated risk" flag; (4) generated a thesis tied to a specific, named causal mechanism (risk-parity cascade amplified by negative dealer gamma) rather than a statistical signal with no attached explanation; (5) sized and timed the hedge accounting for its own market impact on the exact scenario it was designed to protect against, computed inside the same equilibrium solve rather than as an afterthought.

7. RecWM and REN: Product vs. Architecture

RecWM is the product — the continuously-running world model that portfolio managers interact with. REN (Reflexive Equilibrium Networks) is the architecture — the novel model class that makes RecWM computationally possible.

RecWM (Product) REN (Architecture)
What it is A 24/7 financial world model system A new neural network model class
Audience Portfolio managers, CIOs, hedge fund teams ML researchers, financial engineers
Outputs Theses, scenarios, regime alerts, execution plans Equilibrium belief states, bifurcation maps, influence kernels
Measured by P&L contribution, decision quality, PM adoption Convergence speed, equilibrium accuracy, calibration
Analogy Google Maps (the product you use) The routing algorithms + satellite imagery pipeline (the engine underneath)

RecWM could not exist without REN — no existing architecture can compute reflexive belief equilibria as a forward pass. And REN without RecWM is an academic curiosity — a novel model class that doesn't ship anything. They are designed together, but they are not the same thing.

7.1 The Energy-Based Framing (for readers coming from JEPA)

REN can be described in exactly the vocabulary LeCun uses for energy-based world models. Define an energy function over (belief, market-state) pairs, E(b, x) = ||Φ(b; x, θ) − b||² — this is exactly the residual g(b) from Section 3.4, squared. E is low precisely at self-consistent beliefs and high everywhere else, and finding a reflexive equilibrium is finding the minimum of this energy — which is exactly what ATLAS's Anderson-accelerated solver does, minimizing the residual norm rather than merely iterating Φ forward. This is a JEPA-style architecture in a precise sense: there is no attempt to reconstruct raw prices, order books, or news text (the financial equivalent of pixel reconstruction). Belief field vectors Bt ∈ RN×s are the abstract, joint-embedding representation being predicted and matched, and the energy is defined entirely in that abstract space. Where REN departs from typical energy-based JEPA setups is that the energy landscape is not searched by gradient descent toward a single basin — HYDRA (Section 3.6) explicitly maps multiple basins (multiple self-consistent equilibria) and tracks the topology of the energy landscape itself via CONTINUATOR, treating the landscape's bifurcation structure (classified, for low-dimensional parameter slices, by catastrophe theory — fold, cusp, swallowtail, the only generic geometries by Thom's classification theorem) as a first-class object rather than something a single point-estimate optimizer would simply never surface.

7.2 The Evaluation Framing (for readers coming from robotics/embodied AI benchmarking)

A recurring, correct critique of world-model claims in robotics and embodied AI — the kind Fei-Fei Li's spatial-intelligence research program takes seriously — is that "world model" is frequently used loosely, and the honest question is always: evaluated how, and against what null? REN's evaluation surface is deliberately narrow and falsifiable, distinct from RecWM's P&L-facing metrics: (1) equilibrium accuracy — on synthetic belief maps with known closed-form fixed points (Appendix examples in the underlying equilibrium-engine specification), does ATLAS recover b* to a specified tolerance within the claimed iteration budget; (2) convergence speed — measured wall-clock and iteration count against the theoretical rate implied by the observed ρ(DΦ), not against a vague "fast enough" bar; (3) bifurcation detection lead time — on historical regime-change episodes (2008, GameStop, LTCM, the Taper Tantrum, all four discussed in Section 2), does the normalized bifurcation distance δ̂bif cross its warning threshold before, not after, the regime visibly changed in price, and by how much lead time; (4) calibration — do the Boltzmann-weighted equilibrium probabilities {wi} track empirical frequencies when backtested, i.e., is the "probability 0.30" attached to equilibrium B in Section 6 actually well-calibrated across many similar situations, not just plausible-sounding once. None of these four are currently measured (Section 8 is explicit about this) — but stating them precisely, before any results exist, is what separates a testable architecture from a rhetorical one.

8. The Honest Position

RecWM does not exist yet. As of August 2026, it is a design — a detailed architectural specification with mathematical foundations, component designs, data strategies, and build plans. The research on this site documents that design.

What has been done:

  • The mathematical framework for belief equilibria is specified (Influence Kernel, Belief Fields, Equilibrium Engine)
  • The 11 core inventions are designed to component-specification level
  • The data strategy uses only free, publicly available sources
  • The compute requirements are estimated and bounded
  • The competitive landscape is honestly assessed

What has not been done:

  • No code has been written
  • No model has been trained
  • No backtest has been run
  • No live trading has occurred
  • The convergence guarantees are theoretical, not empirical
  • The latency targets (7ms per forward pass) are from complexity analysis, not measurement

8.1 The Minimal Viable Experiment

The smallest experiment that would actually test the central claim — not a full production system, but the narrowest slice that could falsify the architecture — is a single-asset, small-N instantiation: d = 4 (the (μ, σ², γ, κ) belief vector from Section 3.4, Appendix A of the equilibrium-engine specification), N = 4–6 agent types (HFT, CTA, value, retail, market maker), on a single liquid equity index future with a full, freely available tick history. The test sequence: (1) fit the belief-update map Φ and interaction matrix K on a training window; (2) run ATLAS/HYDRA on held-out data and check whether the discovered equilibria are locally stable in the sense the theory predicts (ρ(DΦ) computed independently of the solver, via finite-difference Jacobian, should agree with the solver's internal estimate); (3) check whether SEISMOGRAPH's bifurcation distance, computed walk-forward with no lookahead, gives positive lead time (not merely non-negative, but a specific number of minutes) ahead of at least a handful of known historical volatility regime shifts in that single instrument; (4) check whether the Boltzmann-weighted equilibrium probabilities are calibrated on held-out data via a standard reliability diagram. Failure on (2) would falsify the core fixed-point machinery. Failure on (3) with only look-ahead-free out-of-sample lead time near zero would falsify the central practical claim (Section 4.5) that this is detection, not reaction. This experiment is deliberately small enough to run in weeks, not months, and deliberately structured so that a negative result is informative rather than ambiguous.

8.2 Validation Plan and Timeline

Following the minimal viable experiment, validation proceeds in the same phase structure as the underlying build plan, with an explicit go/no-go gate at each stage rather than a single end-to-end target:

PhaseScopeGo/No-Go Criterion
1. Core solverATLAS on synthetic belief maps with known analytic fixed pointsRecovers b* to specified tolerance in <2ms at d=256; fails cleanly (reports non-convergence, not a wrong answer) when it can't
2. Multiple equilibriaHYDRA + PHANTOM on synthetic systems with known multiplicityFinds all known equilibria in <8ms for 3 equilibria; implicit-differentiation gradients agree with finite-difference gradients away from bifurcation
3. Bifurcation detectionSEISMOGRAPH on the single-asset minimal experiment (Section 8.1) against historical regime shiftsPositive out-of-sample lead time on a majority of tested historical regime-change episodes for that instrument
4. Chaos and integrationFull forward pass, multi-asset, LYAPUNOV SENTINEL integratedEnd-to-end latency within budget; chaos-mode fallback triggers appropriately on known historically chaotic windows rather than misreporting a false equilibrium
5. Paper tradingLive, unfunded, on the validated single-asset (then expanded) instantiationThesis-attributed P&L is separable from market beta and is not explained by the self-impact estimate being systematically wrong in one direction
The gap between design and reality is large. Many well-designed systems fail in implementation. The mathematical framework may prove intractable at scale, the data may be too noisy for reliable belief inference, the equilibrium computation may be too slow for real-time operation, and the entire reflexive-equilibrium premise may turn out to be less useful than simpler approaches. This site documents the design and the reasoning behind it. It does not claim that RecWM works. That claim requires building it — starting with the minimal viable experiment above, not the full seven-fragment, multi-asset system, and with explicit willingness to be falsified at any of the five phase gates.

9. Competitive Architecture Comparison — Deep Technical

Section 1.2 sketched the four canonical world-model lineages in broad strokes. This section goes down to the equations. The purpose is not rhetorical — it is falsifiable engineering comparison. For each system, the exact update rule is written out, its published results are stated without editorializing, and the specific architectural reason it cannot compute a reflexive equilibrium is derived from its own equations rather than asserted. If RecWM's central claim is wrong — if one of these architectures already solves the reflexivity problem — that should be visible directly in the math below, not hidden behind a marketing comparison table.

9.1 DreamerV3 (Hafner et al., Nature, April 2025)

DreamerV3 is the most mature and most widely deployed world-model architecture in existence, with a single fixed configuration validated across more than 150 tasks spanning Atari, DeepMind Lab, Minecraft, and continuous control, plus 2024–2025 industrial deployments (fusion-reactor plasma control at TCV, chip-floorplanning at Google). Its core is a Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM):

ht = fGRU(ht−1, zt−1, at−1)     (deterministic recurrence)
zt ∼ pφ(zt | ht)     (prior, used for imagination)
zt ∼ qφ(zt | ht, xt)     (posterior, used for training)

Training minimizes a three-part loss with explicit KL balancing and free bits to prevent posterior collapse:

L(φ) = Lpred + 0.5·Ldyn + 0.1·Lrep

where Lpred reconstructs observations, rewards, and episode continuation; Ldyn pulls the prior toward the (stop-gradiented) posterior; Lrep pulls the posterior toward the (stop-gradiented) prior, at a tenth of the weight, which is the specific mechanism that stabilizes training across wildly different reward scales without per-task tuning. Two further engineering choices make the "one config for everything" claim work: symlog normalization of all inputs and targets (symlog(x) = sign(x)·log(|x|+1)), and twohot discrete regression of scalar values onto 255 exponentially-spaced bins rather than direct scalar regression, which handles the heavy-tailed reward distributions that appear in some of the 150+ tasks (Atari's occasional huge score jumps look structurally like a fat-tailed P&L distribution). DreamerV3 was also the first algorithm to autonomously collect diamonds in Minecraft from scratch, without human data or curricula — a genuinely hard long-horizon sparse-reward planning problem solved entirely inside imagined rollouts.

Where it fails at reflexivity, from the equations themselves. The RSSM's transition zt ∼ pφ(zt | ht) is a single stochastic map with no dependence on any other agent's model of the same environment, and no term through which the agent's own value estimate or policy feeds back into the physics being modeled. This is correct for Atari, Minecraft, and plasma control — the environment genuinely does not care what Dreamer believes about it. It is the wrong architecture for markets, because T(s,a;B) in Section 1.4 is parameterized by the belief field that generates the very actions feeding the transition. There is no slot in the RSSM for B. Bolting a belief field onto the recurrent state ht would not fix this: DreamerV3's actor-critic is trained entirely on single-agent imagined rollouts through pφ, which has no mechanism for computing a self-consistency fixed point across multiple interacting belief-holders, only for autoregressive forward sampling. It is a superb single-agent, stationary-dynamics world model. Financial markets are neither single-agent nor stationary in the relevant sense (Section 1.4).

9.2 MuZero (Schrittwieser et al., Nature, 2020)

MuZero learns three networks rather than reconstructing observations at all:

Representation:   h : o1:t → s0
Dynamics:   g : (sk, ak) → (sk+1, rk+1)
Prediction:   f : sk → (pk, vk)

and plans with Monte Carlo Tree Search entirely inside this learned latent space, guided by the value-equivalence principle: the latent dynamics g is trained not to reconstruct s accurately, but only so that value, policy, and reward predictions built on top of it are accurate — a strictly weaker and more efficient training signal than pixel reconstruction. This let MuZero match AlphaZero's superhuman play in Go, chess, and shogi without ever being told the rules of the game, and achieve superhuman Atari performance from the same architecture. It is the strongest existing demonstration that a world model does not need to be representationally complete, only decision-sufficient — the same discipline RecWM inherits for its belief field (Section 1.2).

Where it fails at reflexivity. MuZero's action space is discrete (or discretized), its self-play setting is explicitly two-player zero-sum with a known, stationary game tree (chess's rules do not change because MuZero plays well), and MCTS as a planning algorithm is structurally suited to tree search over discrete branching, not to solving a continuous fixed-point equation like Φ(b*) = b*. There is no mechanism in MuZero for "many agents simultaneously updating beliefs about a continuous state that all of their combined actions jointly determine" — the entire framework assumes turn-taking, not simultaneous market clearing. Applying MuZero to markets would require either discretizing the action space so coarsely that meaningful portfolio construction becomes impossible, or replacing MCTS with a different planner entirely — at which point what remains is only the representation/dynamics/prediction factorization, not the algorithm that made MuZero work.

9.3 Ha & Schmidhuber, "World Models" (2018)

The foundational paper of the modern lineage, and still the cleanest illustration of the perception/dynamics/control separation. A convolutional VAE (4 conv layers, 32- or 64-dimensional latent z) compresses raw frames; an MDN-RNN (an LSTM whose output parameterizes a mixture of 5 Gaussians) predicts P(zt+1 | zt, at, ht); a linear controller with only 867 parameters, optimized by CMA-ES (an evolutionary strategy, not gradient descent), maps [zt, ht] directly to an action. The controller is trained entirely by "dreaming" — rolling out inside the MDN-RNN with an elevated temperature parameter τ = 1.15, which deliberately injects extra stochasticity into imagined rollouts so the controller cannot exploit deterministic quirks of the learned dynamics that would not hold in the real environment. This produced a score of 906 on CarRacing-v0 (state of the art at publication) and, more strikingly, a VizDoom agent trained entirely inside the dream, never touching the real simulator during training, that transferred successfully to the real game.

Where it fails at reflexivity. The VAE is unsupervised — it compresses whatever visual features have high reconstruction variance, with no mechanism to prioritize task-relevant or belief-relevant structure over irrelevant visual detail (this is precisely the "grass texture" problem JEPA was designed to fix, Section 9.4). The architecture is single-agent by construction: the controller has no notion that other controllers exist, let alone that their beliefs about the environment jointly determine the environment's next state. And the entire capacity budget is tiny (867 controller parameters) by design, appropriate for a low-dimensional driving task, wholly inadequate for representing a belief field Bt ∈ RN×s across dozens of agent types and hundreds of instruments. It is the right blueprint for the separation of concerns RecWM's Observe/Infer/Compute-Equilibrium/Predict/Act loop inherits (Section 1.2), and the wrong architecture to extend directly.

9.4 JEPA and the LeCun Program (2022–2026)

JEPA (Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) is the most philosophically adjacent prior art to RecWM's belief field, and the one most worth engaging seriously rather than dismissing. The framework is energy-based: define a scalar compatibility function

Fw(x, y) = minz Ew(x, y, z)

that is low when y is a plausible continuation of context x and high otherwise, with a latent z minimized out to capture the (possibly multi-modal) space of plausible continuations. Critically, JEPA is non-generative: it never reconstructs y in pixel space, only predicts an abstract embedding of it, produced by an exponential-moving-average (EMA) target encoder that is never trained directly by gradient descent (only by tracking the online encoder), which prevents the trivial collapse solution (encoder maps everything to a constant). A second anti-collapse mechanism, VICReg (Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization), explicitly penalizes the embedding covariance matrix for having low-rank structure. LeCun's full proposal is a 6-module cognitive architecture — Configurator, Perception, World Model, Cost, Actor, Short-Term Memory — of which JEPA instantiates only the World Model module.

The empirical program has moved fast. I-JEPA (CVPR 2023) demonstrated roughly 10x greater training efficiency than masked autoencoding (MAE) for the same downstream linear-probe accuracy. V-JEPA 2, released June 2025, scaled to 1.2B parameters trained on over 1 million hours of video and demonstrated zero-shot robot manipulation — a robot arm executing pick-and-place tasks in environments it had never seen, using JEPA embeddings for planning without any task-specific fine-tuning. LeCun left Meta in late 2025 to found AMI Labs, which raised a reported $1.03B seed round in March 2026 explicitly to pursue "world models over language models" as the next architecture generation. Since 2023 the JEPA family has fragmented into more than 30 published variants spanning vision, audio, 3D scene understanding, autonomous driving, medical imaging, and time series — including, most relevantly, Fin-JEPA (May 2026), the first published financial-domain JEPA: 367K parameters trained across 6,230 equities, predicting return-relevant embeddings rather than raw price paths. The generative variant D-JEPA and the causally-structured Causal-JEPA (ICML 2026) are both explicit attempts to push the framework toward causal and interventional reasoning.

Where it fails at reflexivity — the most important comparison in this section. JEPA is a representation-learning framework for perception: it answers "what is the best abstract embedding of this context for predicting this target," and it does so extremely well, non-generatively, at scale. It is not a framework for reflexive equilibrium, and the gap is structural, not a matter of scaling further or adding a financial-domain variant. Three specific absences:

  • No self-impact layer. Nothing in the energy function E(x,y,z) represents the fact that the model computing the embedding is itself an actor whose predictions, once acted on, change the distribution generating y. JEPA embeddings are learned assuming y is exogenous to the model's own inference.
  • No mechanism for the model being inside the system it models. Fin-JEPA predicts return-relevant embeddings of equities; it has no representation of a fund using Fin-JEPA's own outputs to trade those same equities, which is precisely the case that matters for a hedge fund deploying such a model at scale (Section 4, self-impact estimation).
  • No fixed-point solver. JEPA's forward pass is a single feedforward prediction (context embedding → predicted target embedding). There is no iterative self-consistency computation of the kind ATLAS/HYDRA perform (Equilibrium Computation Engine, Sections 1–2) — nothing in the architecture asks "does this predicted embedding, once acted upon by the population of agents it describes, regenerate itself."

The honest framing is complementary, not competitive: a JEPA-style non-generative encoder is a plausible component for RecWM's Observe stage — compressing raw market observations into representation space before belief inference — but the belief field, the equilibrium fixed point, and the bifurcation monitor sit entirely outside anything the JEPA literature has published or attempted as of mid-2026.

9.5 MarS — Microsoft's Large Market Model (ICLR 2025)

MarS is the closest thing to a direct competitor that currently exists, and it deserves the most careful treatment. It is an order-level generative foundation model for financial markets, built from two complementary components. The Order Sequence Model is a causal transformer trained autoregressively on individual orders conditioned on limit-order-book state, scaled to 1.02B parameters trained on 32B tokens of order-level data. The Order-Batch Sequence Model operates at a coarser granularity, autoregressively generating minute-level order batches, scaled to 3B parameters trained on 10B tokens. Both feed into a simulated clearing house that matches generated orders against the book, producing closed-loop feedback: the simulator's own matching engine determines what price the generated orders clear at, and that price becomes context for the next generation step. MarS explicitly validates against the empirical Square-Root Law of market impact (price impact scales with the square root of order size relative to volume) and reproduces 9 of 11 canonical stylized facts of real market microstructure — fat tails in returns, volatility clustering, and long-memory in order flow among them.

Where it falls short of a reflexive world model. MarS learns statistical correlations in order-flow sequences well enough to reproduce microstructure stylized facts; it does not learn or compute an equilibrium structure over agent beliefs. Its "reflexivity" is exactly one mechanism deep: the mechanical feedback of generated-order-clears-at-a-price, which then conditions the next generation step. This is real feedback, but it is not strategic feedback — there is no belief-holding agent inside MarS whose model of other agents' beliefs changes its own action in the way Section 3.4's belief update map Uθ requires. There is no performative-prediction layer (Section 4) accounting for the fact that a fund using MarS's own forecasts to trade would change the distribution MarS is forecasting. Validation is restricted to Chinese A-share market data; the pretrained weights have not been released, only the simulation framework; and production-scale generation for a full trading day is reported to require on the order of 128 GPUs, which is a materially different compute posture than the millisecond-latency, single-machine-class target in Section 3 (REN's ~7ms forward pass). MarS is the most credible existing proof that order-level generative modeling of markets is tractable at scale. It is not a system that computes reflexive equilibria, monitors bifurcation, or reasons about the strategic interaction of belief-holding agents.

9.6 EWM — Equilibrium World Models (Schaab & Scheidegger, 2026)

EWM is discussed at length elsewhere in this document (the EWM Field Landscape memo; Section 8's related work), and is the closest thing in the academic literature to RecWM's actual mathematical object — a deep-learning method for globally solving dynamic stochastic economic models by finding fixed points of policy and value functions. Its architecture has six components: a policy network πθ, an exact transition operator Γ (not learned — taken directly from the model's known structural equations), a structural residual R whose minimization is the training objective, a coverage measure μκ combining the model's ergodic distribution with deliberately added stress states and local perturbations (so the network is trained on more than just the states the model visits in equilibrium), a world component Wψ, and an exact-residual audit that checks the trained solution against the model's true equilibrium conditions rather than trusting the loss curve. On heterogeneous-agent models with high-dimensional wealth distributions, EWM achieves roughly 25x compression relative to standard grid-based global solution methods, while maintaining accuracy against the exact residual audit.

Where it falls short of a market simulator. EWM requires the researcher to write down the structural equations of the economic model in advance — the utility functions, budget constraints, market-clearing conditions — and then uses deep learning purely as a fast global solver for the resulting fixed-point system. It is, in the terminology of this document, structurally consistent by construction: reflexivity is handled correctly because the model's equations already encode the feedback loop. But it cannot ingest raw market data and learn the structural equations from observation, it cannot backtest a discretionary trading strategy against historical price action, and — as the EWM Field Landscape memo notes — its scalability upper bound as state-space dimension grows has not been established in the published work. RecWM's REN component (Sections 3.4–3.9, and the Equilibrium Computation Engine specification) is architecturally closer to EWM than to any of the deep-RL world models above — ATLAS/HYDRA/SEISMOGRAPH are, in EWM's own vocabulary, a policy network plus exact-residual monitoring — but RecWM's belief field is learned from data rather than derived from hand-specified utility functions, which is the tradeoff of practical usability against theoretical guarantees discussed in Section 9.8 below.

9.7 TwinMarket (NeurIPS 2025 / ICLR 2025 Best Paper recognition)

TwinMarket takes the opposite approach from EWM: instead of solving equations, it simulates 1,000 LLM-powered agents, each instantiated with a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) cognitive architecture, individually parameterized cognitive biases (overconfidence, recency bias, herding susceptibility), and emotional-state variables that fluctuate in response to simulated gains and losses. Run forward, the population of interacting LLM agents produces emergent bubbles and crashes without those dynamics being hand-coded anywhere — the boom-bust cycle is a genuinely emergent property of 1,000 agents with realistic psychological biases trading against each other.

Where it falls short as a production system. The computational cost of running 1,000 LLM inference calls per simulated timestep is prohibitive for real-time or even near-real-time operation at trading speed. There are no mathematical guarantees of any kind — no convergence proof, no stability characterization, no way to certify that a given emergent bubble in simulation corresponds to a specific real-market mechanism rather than an artifact of the particular LLM's biases. Population diversity is fragile: if the underlying LLM's outputs are insufficiently varied across the 1,000 agent instantiations, the simulation risks collapsing toward homogeneous behavior that does not actually reproduce heterogeneous-agent dynamics. And because the reflexivity is emergent rather than analytically derived, there is no SEISMOGRAPH-equivalent (Section 3.7) — no way to compute a bifurcation distance or a spectral radius, because there is no explicit belief-update Jacobian to differentiate. TwinMarket is the most vivid existing demonstration that reflexive dynamics can emerge from realistic agent population simulation. It is not a system anyone could deploy for millisecond-latency bifurcation monitoring on a live book.

9.8 The Gap RecWM Fills

Line the seven systems up against two independent axes and the gap becomes visible geometrically rather than rhetorically. Call a system structurally consistent if it handles reflexivity analytically — if feedback between beliefs/predictions and the state being predicted is represented in the model's equations, not merely observed as an emergent artifact of simulation. Call a system practically usable if it can ingest real market data, run at trading-relevant latency, and support strategy backtesting and deployment.

No system published in the 2024–2026 literature is both structurally consistent and practically usable as a market simulator for strategy development. EWM is structurally consistent (reflexivity is in the equations) but requires hand-specified structural models and has no backtesting interface. MarS is practically usable (ingests real order data, runs a simulated clearing engine) but its reflexivity is one mechanical feedback loop deep, with no strategic belief layer and no performative-prediction accounting. TwinMarket produces structurally rich emergent reflexivity but at LLM-population cost with zero mathematical guarantees. DreamerV3, MuZero, Ha & Schmidhuber, and JEPA are all, by their own authors' framing, built for environments whose dynamics are exogenous to the agent's beliefs — the assumption that fails for markets by construction (Section 1.4). This is precisely the gap RecWM is designed to fill: a belief field learned from real market data (practical usability, like MarS and the RL world models), computing equilibria and monitoring bifurcation via a differentiable fixed-point solver with convergence and stability guarantees (structural consistency, like EWM), with a self-impact estimator accounting for the fund's own footprint (performative prediction, which none of the seven systems above implement end-to-end).

10. Cross-Domain Validation Parallels

An architecture that only makes sense when described in its own vocabulary is a warning sign. The strongest evidence that RecWM's design choices are not arbitrary is that the same choices, in different language, are already load-bearing in two domains that have spent decades under far more severe consequences for getting real-time state estimation wrong: electric grid operations and submarine warfare. Neither domain is a metaphor bolted on after the fact — both are documented in full elsewhere in this dossier (the power-grid and submarine-intelligence parallels) and are summarized here specifically for what they validate about RecWM's architecture, not as color.

10.1 The Power Grid Parallel — State Estimation, Contingency Analysis, and Silent Failure

A regional transmission organization's Energy Management System solves, continuously, the same class of problem RecWM's Observe/Infer stages solve: reconstruct the true, unobservable state of a large interconnected system from a bounded set of noisy measurements. The grid's state estimator minimizes J(x) = [z − h(x)]TR−1[z − h(x)] — a weighted least-squares fit of a nonlinear measurement model to telemetry — and, critically, performs explicit bad-data detection: measurements with abnormally large normalized residuals are flagged and excluded rather than silently blended in. Four specific design principles transfer directly:

  • Observability, not omniscience. A large RTO does not instrument every point in the grid; it places measurements strategically so the system's Jacobian has full rank and the state is uniquely determined. RecWM's data strategy (Section 6, and the free-data architecture referenced in Section 8) makes the identical bet: a bounded set of strategically chosen public signals — yield curves, credit spread curves, volatility surfaces, funding spreads, flow proxies — is claimed to make the belief field observable without requiring the unobservable ground truth (actual positioning, actual leverage) that no market participant has access to.
  • Contingency analysis as preventive security, not reactive stress testing. The N-1/N-2/N-1-1 hierarchy runs thousands of what-if power-flow solutions continuously, acting on violations before the contingency occurs, not after. HYDRA's multi-equilibrium search (Equilibrium Computation Engine, Section 2) and SEISMOGRAPH's bifurcation-distance monitor (Section 3) are the same discipline applied to belief space: find every equilibrium the market could coordinate on, not just the one it currently occupies, and measure the distance to the nearest structural failure continuously rather than discovering it after the fact.
  • Never fail silently. The single most consequential lesson of the 2003 Northeast Blackout is that the state estimator and alarm system both died quietly, with the displays frozen and appearing normal, and operators made decisions on stale data for over an hour without knowing it. The financial-system analogue is 2007–2008: Gaussian-copula-based CDO risk models kept producing confident, wrong numbers as the correlation structure they assumed broke down. RecWM's chaos-mode graceful degradation (LYAPUNOV SENTINEL, Equilibrium Computation Engine Section 5.4) is a direct structural response to this lesson — when the Lyapunov exponent indicates no stable equilibrium exists, the system is required to say so explicitly (attractor statistics, entropy, fragility score) rather than silently reporting a stale or spuriously converged fixed point.
  • Frequency as the single vital-sign number. Grid frequency — one scalar — tells an operator, in under a second, whether generation and load are in balance system-wide. RecWM's spectral-radius diagnostic ρ(DΦ) (Section 2.3) is proposed as the financial equivalent: a single, continuously computed number that says whether the belief-price loop is currently self-correcting or self-reinforcing, displayed with the same prominence a grid operator gives frequency, not buried in a report.

10.2 The Submarine Intelligence Parallel — Fusion, Classification, and Blind-Spot Discipline

A submarine has no windows; its picture of the world is built entirely from indirect, ambiguous, multi-sensor fragments — passive sonar bearings, ESM intercepts, periscope glimpses, fleet broadcast intelligence — fused through a discipline that predates and directly parallels the multi-source belief inference RecWM performs. Four elements of that discipline map onto specific RecWM design commitments:

  • Bearing-only observations require triangulation over time, not a single high-fidelity reading. A single sonar bearing tells you direction, not range or identity; Target Motion Analysis triangulates a firing solution from multiple bearings collected across maneuvers. RecWM's belief inference is built on the same premise: no single data source (not even a comprehensive one) determines the market's belief state. A credit spread widening 15bp is a bearing-only contact — ambiguous until corroborated by FX vol, funding spreads, and flow data collected from independent vantage points, exactly as the submarine fuses sonar, ESM, and periscope observations of different physical character before committing to a classification.
  • Continuous track files with confidence levels, not point-in-time snapshots. A submarine's track file on a contact is a living object — classification, course, speed, and confidence all update as new evidence arrives, and reclassification (idiosyncratic stress becomes systemic contagion) is explicit and logged. This is structurally identical to CONTINUATOR's equilibrium-landscape data structure (Equilibrium Computation Engine, Section 6.3), which maintains a persistent, time-indexed record of every equilibrium branch — birth, evolution, death — rather than reporting only the currently converged solution.
  • The baffles check — systematic, scheduled blind-spot discovery. A submarine's own propulsion noise masks the sector directly astern, so the doctrine is a periodic, forced maneuver to clear it — not an occasional convenience but a non-negotiable operating procedure whose frequency scales with threat level. RecWM's contingency scanning (drawing the same discipline from the grid's N-1 analysis in Section 10.1) is designed as the equivalent: systematically surfacing exposures a portfolio manager is not explicitly watching — second- and third-order correlations through supply chains, funding markets, and cross-asset channels — on a forced schedule, not only when a human happens to think to check.
  • Never let one sensor dominate the picture. The doctrine that sinks submarines is fixating on the sonar operator's confident contact while ignoring the ESM board. The doctrine that RecWM's fragment architecture (Section 3, and the seven-fragment structure referenced across this document) is built to prevent is the financial equivalent: a belief field that weights price data, flow data, fundamental data, and text/sentiment data through a principled fusion mechanism rather than any single high-frequency source dominating the state estimate by virtue of being the easiest to obtain.

10.3 Why These Parallels Validate the Architecture Rather Than Merely Decorate It

The value of these two parallels is not that grids and submarines are "like" markets in some loose sense — it is that both domains arrived at their current operating doctrine only after catastrophic, well-documented failures (the 2003 blackout; the doctrine refinements that followed decades of Cold War close calls), and both domains have had those doctrines stress-tested under conditions far more unforgiving than a hedge fund's daily P&L. A grid operator who fails to observe a bad-data flag can black out 55 million people in 90 seconds. A submarine commander who fails a baffles check can lose the boat. When systems refined under that kind of pressure converge independently on the same structural principles — strategic (not exhaustive) observability, continuous rather than periodic state estimation, explicit uncertainty reporting rather than silent degradation, and forced systematic blind-spot discovery — that convergence is evidence about which architectural properties actually matter for real-time state estimation under adversarial, high-stakes conditions, independent of the specific physics of the domain. RecWM's design choices in Sections 3–5 were made to satisfy the same properties. The parallels are the argument that those properties are the right ones to target, not proof that RecWM currently satisfies them at production quality.

11. The Research Frontier

Section 8 already states plainly that no code has been written, no model trained, and no live trading has occurred. This section is more specific about exactly what remains unproven, why it remains unproven (i.e., what is actually hard about it, not just "we haven't gotten to it yet"), and how RecWM's roadmap connects to the broader academic field that only received a name in August 2026.

11.1 What Remains to Be Proven

11.2 The Validation Roadmap, Restated as a Falsification Ladder

Section 8.2's five-phase plan is a build sequence. Read as a falsification ladder, it has a specific property worth making explicit: each phase is designed so a negative result kills the project at that phase rather than being absorbed and rationalized. Phase 1 (core solver) tests pure numerics against known analytic answers — if ATLAS cannot recover a known fixed point on a synthetic map, nothing downstream matters. Phase 2 (multiple equilibria) tests whether HYDRA's deflation and PHANTOM's implicit differentiation are correct on systems with known multiplicity — a mathematical correctness gate, not an economic one. Phase 3 (bifurcation detection) is the first phase that touches real market data and the first phase where "it works mathematically but is useless in practice" becomes a live possibility — this is deliberately the smallest possible real-data test (Section 8.1's single-instrument, small-N setup), specifically so a failure here is informative rather than confounded by scale. Phase 4 integrates chaos detection and multi-asset scope. Phase 5 is unfunded paper trading with an explicit requirement that attributed P&L survive the self-impact correction, not just look good in aggregate. The ladder is designed so the project can die honestly at any rung, which is the opposite of how most trading-system research is structured (build the full system, then discover in production that a foundational assumption was wrong).

11.3 Connection to the EWM Field — Named August 2026

The academic field most structurally adjacent to RecWM's REN component — equilibrium world models for economic systems — only received a settled name in the literature in August 2026, with Schaab & Scheidegger's EWM paper (Section 9.6) serving as the reference architecture the emerging field organizes around. This matters for two reasons beyond nomenclature. First, it means the field's benchmark suite, evaluation conventions, and shared terminology are still being established in real time — there is no equivalent yet of the standardized task suites (Atari-100k, the DMLab-30 suite, Procgen) that let DreamerV3 and MuZero be compared apples-to-apples across published results. RecWM's own validation (Section 11.2) cannot currently be benchmarked against a field-standard suite because one does not yet exist; the minimal viable experiment (Section 8.1) is, by necessity, a bespoke evaluation rather than a submission to an established leaderboard. Second, and more specifically: the L1–L6 capability ladder referenced elsewhere in this dossier (from Han et al., "From Economic Agents to Agentic Economies") currently has an empty L6 rung — the level corresponding to a fully autonomous, self-consistent agentic economy simulator. No published system, including EWM, TwinMarket, or MarS, currently occupies L6. RecWM's stated ambition sits at that empty rung. Naming a field before its top capability level has a single occupant is normal — it happened with world models in robotics well before DreamerV3 — but it is worth being explicit that RecWM would be attempting to fill a gap the field itself has only just finished defining, not executing a known playbook.

11.4 The Interventional Benchmark Gap

The single most consequential missing piece in the entire adjacent literature — EWM included — is an interventional benchmark: a standardized, public evaluation that tests whether a model's counterfactual predictions (Section 1.1's "what would happen under an action never taken") are actually correct, as opposed to merely testing whether a model's forward predictions match realized outcomes. Every benchmark referenced in this document — Atari-100k, the Minecraft diamond task, MarS's stylized-fact reproduction, EWM's exact-residual audit — evaluates a system against data the system was allowed to observe unfold, or against equations whose ground truth is known by construction. None of them evaluate whether a system correctly predicts what would have happened under a policy that was never actually run.

This gap is not a minor omission; it is arguably the reason reflexivity has been under-addressed in the world-model literature at all. A benchmark built from historical data can only ever validate observational accuracy — does the model's forward rollout match what actually happened — because historical data by definition contains only the one action sequence that actually occurred. Perdomo et al.'s performative-prediction framework (Theorem 3.5, cited throughout this document's discussion of the ε < γ/β stability condition) is a theoretical result precisely because no dataset exists on which it could currently be tested empirically at scale: verifying it requires observing the same underlying population under multiple different deployed models, which requires either genuine A/B deployment (expensive, risky, rarely done in finance) or a simulator faithful enough that counterfactual deployment inside the simulator is trustworthy — which is circular unless the simulator's own counterfactual fidelity has independently been validated.

This is the sharpest open problem RecWM inherits from the field, not one it has solved. The minimal viable experiment (Section 8.1) sidesteps the interventional benchmark gap rather than closing it — it tests observational accuracy (does the discovered equilibrium match the theory's predictions on held-out data, does the bifurcation warning precede a regime change that actually happened) because that is what is currently testable without live deployment. It does not test whether RecWM's counterfactual predictions about actions never taken are correct, because no benchmark for that exists yet, for RecWM or for any system referenced in Section 9. Phase 5's paper-trading validation is the closest approximation available — a live, unfunded deployment is the one setting where the model's own actions genuinely do or do not feed back into the state it is modeling, which is the only way to test the self-impact estimator (Section 4) against reality rather than against a simulator's assumptions about reality. Until an interventional benchmark exists for financial world models generally, every claim in this document about counterfactual accuracy should be read as a design target the architecture is built to make testable eventually, not a result.

The Triple Correspondence

The core architectural insight: three independently-motivated diagnostics, developed in three unrelated literatures, converge on the same mathematical object.

ρ(DΦ(b*)) < 1
one spectral radius — three domains of meaning
DEQ Convergence
The fixed-point iteration in ATLAS contracts and converges when the Jacobian's spectral radius is below 1 — standard deep equilibrium theory (Bai et al. 2019).
Perdomo Stability
Performative predictions remain stable, not self-defeating, exactly when ε < γ/β — the performative-prediction stability condition (Perdomo et al. 2020, Thm. 3.5).
Scheffer Critical Slowing
As ρ(DΦ) → 1, recovery from perturbation slows — the early-warning signal for critical transitions (Scheffer et al. 2009).

When ρ(DΦ) < 1: the solver converges, predictions are performatively stable, and the regime is robust. When ρ(DΦ) → 1: convergence slows, performative predictions become self-defeating, and a regime transition approaches. One number governs all three phenomena — which is why SEISMOGRAPH's eigenvalue tracker doubles as both a solver-health monitor and a regime-change early-warning system.

The Always-On World Model

Your Portfolio Never Sleeps.
Your Understanding of the
World Shouldn’t Either.

RecWM is not a prediction engine. It is a 24/7 situational awareness system that reads the current state of the entire financial world, understands what it means for your book, and monitors continuously so you can act with conviction instead of anxiety.

Synthesised from 10 deep-research perspectives: veteran portfolio manager, military strategist, trauma surgeon, submarine commander, NASA flight controller, sports analyst, chess grandmaster, behavioral psychologist, power grid engineer, and cultural anthropologist.

The Weight of the Book

People outside this business think portfolio management is about being smart. It is not. It is about carrying weight. The weight of knowing that while you sleep, someone in Tokyo or Frankfurt is doing something that could make your quarter or destroy your year.

“My phone is always on the nightstand. Face down so the screen light does not wake my wife. I have trained myself to do a half-conscious check — roll over, tap the screen, squint at S&P futures, squint at dollar-yen, squint at the 10-year. If something has moved, I am awake. Fully, completely, horribly awake. This happens three to four nights a week.”

— Macro PM, 25 years, former Soros Fund Management / Brevan Howard

THE SUNDAY OPEN

Every Sunday at 6pm Eastern, CME futures open. Every PM checks. At barbecues. At funerals. At their daughter’s college move-in. There is a seven-second window between tapping the phone and seeing the number where the stomach is in free fall.

THE 3AM MOSAIC

The PM builds a mental mosaic from 50 weak signals every day — a Reuters headline, a prime broker’s tone of voice, order flow in the first 30 minutes, a taxi driver mentioning crypto. This mosaic lives entirely in their head. It is not written down, not systematic, not verifiable.

RecWM carries this weight for the PM. Not by replacing their judgment — by ensuring they never have to be the only one watching.

What 24/7 Awareness Actually Means

RecWM does not predict the future. It understands the present — deeply, continuously, across every market, every timezone, every signal — so the PM can make the best possible move given the current state of the world.

Analogy How They Monitor 24/7 RecWM Parallel
ICU Monitor 700–1,500 data points/hour across dozens of vital signs. Nurses read patterns across signals, not individual numbers. 7 fragments monitored continuously. Cross-fragment patterns (liquidity + credit + structure) detected before they appear in price.

Three Levels of Situational Awareness

Dr. Mica Endsley’s model of situational awareness, developed for fighter pilots, defines the gap RecWM fills:

LEVEL 1 — PERCEPTION

Bloomberg

Sees every blip on the radar. Shows prices, spreads, yields, headlines. A magnificent sensor — but it does not tell you which blip is going to kill you.

LEVEL 2 — COMPREHENSION

Sell-Side Research

Understands what individual data points mean. Usually two days late, from an analyst covering 40 names. An intelligence briefing about yesterday’s battle.

LEVEL 3 — PROJECTION

RecWM

Projects the future state of the environment from current comprehension. Knows that the recession trade will force systematic funds to de-lever in 3 days, creating a predictable window of forced selling.

EXAMPLE: SVB COLLAPSE, MARCH 2023
Level 1 (Bloomberg): SVB stock down 60%. Depositors withdrawing.
Level 2 (Analyst): Duration mismatch. Classic bank run. First Republic vulnerable.
Level 3 (RecWM): Flight to quality → 2Y yield compresses 50-80bps in 48hrs. Fed forced to pause. CDS widens 30-50bps. Contagion contained to regionals — large banks are beneficiaries. Optimal trade: long 2Y Treasuries, long NASDAQ, short KRE, 72-hour horizon.

Reading the World from Fragments

A submarine has no windows. It constructs its picture of reality from fragments of sound — passive sonar bearings that are individually ambiguous but collectively powerful. A hedge fund operates the same way: it sees fragments of market reality and must infer the full picture.

Bearing-Only Contacts

A credit spread widening 15bps is a bearing-only contact. You know something is out there. Is it idiosyncratic? A forced seller? Or the leading edge of a systemic crisis? A single data point is nearly useless. RecWM collects bearings from every market — FX vol, cross-currency basis, repo rates, shipping data — and triangulates the real signal.

The Baffles Check

Submarines have a blind spot directly behind them where propulsion noise masks incoming sound. They must periodically turn to “clear their baffles.” RecWM does this for the PM: “You are monitoring US equities and rates, but your portfolio has exposure to EM credit through supply chain positions. That’s in your baffles right now.”

“The submarine commander who has operated with full sensor integration never wants to surface. Surfacing feels naked and exposed — you lose the sonar picture, you lose stealth, you’re visible to everyone. The PM who operates with a world model’s integrated picture will feel the same way going back to Bloomberg. Suddenly blind, exposed, vulnerable.”

— Retired US Navy submarine commander, 26 years

The Golden Hour

In trauma medicine, the first 60 minutes after injury determine survival. R. Adams Cowley showed that patients receiving surgical care within the golden hour had dramatically better outcomes. Each 10-minute delay increases mortality by 3.6%.

In finance, the first 60 minutes after a regime shift determine whether you lose 2% or 20%.

The Portfolio Is a Patient

A portfolio has vital signs. It can deteriorate suddenly. It needs 24/7 monitoring. And early detection saves capital the same way it saves lives.

The Portfolio Health Score

Hospitals use Early Warning Scores (NEWS2) — a single number aggregating multiple vital signs. A score of 7+ predicts cardiac arrest better than any individual vital sign. RecWM creates the same: a continuously-updated composite score integrating all 7 fragments.

Alarm Fatigue: The Silent Killer

ICU monitors generate 187 alarms per bed per day. 85–99% are false positives. Nurses respond to only 2–12% of them. RecWM avoids this by surfacing contextualised assessments, not raw alerts. Not “VIX is up 2 points” but “the combination of dealer gamma flipping short + credit widening + funding stress suggests a regime transition with 40% probability in 5 days. Your conditional expected drawdown is -3.8%.”

Why They’ll Never Give It Up

This is not about features. It is about a psychological transformation so deep that going back feels like losing a limb.

Extended Cognition

Clark & Chalmers (1998): tools become literal extensions of the mind. A blind person’s cane becomes part of their perceptual system. RecWM becomes part of how the PM perceives markets. Removing it is cognitive amputation, not inconvenience.

Safety-Level Attachment

Maslow: safety needs are more fundamental than esteem. The PM’s deepest anxiety is “what am I missing?” RecWM addresses this at the most fundamental level. Products that address safety needs create the deepest, most irrational attachment — like baby monitors and home security.

The Guardian Angel

The system maps onto the cross-cultural archetype of the tireless protector. CGM research (Polonsky et al. 2017): patients describe continuous monitors in protective, almost parental terms. The PM will describe RecWM the same way — “it watches over my book.”

Flow State Unlock

Csikszentmihalyi: flow requires surrendering vigilance, which is irrational without monitoring. RecWM enables delegation of vigilance — the PM can focus on strategic thinking because the system handles surveillance. ATC studies show 2.3× more frequent flow with automated conflict detection.

The Nurse Who Can Never Go Back

An ICU nurse who has worked with continuous electronic monitoring will never return to manual four-hourly charting. Not because they can’t — they did it for 20 years. But because they now know what they were missing. They know about the patients who deteriorated between checks. They know about the lactate trend at 3am that caught the slow bleeder. That knowledge cannot be un-known. The PM who has used RecWM will undergo the same transformation. Going back to Bloomberg + gut feel will feel like going back to paper charts. The anxiety of the gaps returns, and it is unbearable.

What the PM Actually Wants

1. Reads everything I read, plus everything I cannot read. Every signal that has ever mattered — shipping data, satellite imagery, power consumption in Chinese provinces, job postings at central banks, credit card aggregates, app download trends. Everything. All the time.

2. Synthesises, not summarises. “Copper is down 3% but Chilean miners are up. Last time: March 2018, preceded a 6-week rally. Meanwhile Chinese credit impulse turned positive and LME warehouse stocks are declining. Your short copper position may be offside.” That is synthesis.

3. Knows my book and talks to me about it. Knows my positions, my P&L, my risk limits. Knows I hold losers too long and cut winners too early. Uses all of this to contextualise every insight.

4. Tells me what changed, not what is. A change log, not a summary. What moved that should not have? What did not move that should have?

5. Argues with me. Steelmans the other side. Forces me to confront the possibility I am wrong, and specifically how I would know if I were wrong.

“I want my brain, but better. I want the synthesis I do — the mosaic building, the pattern recognition — done by something that never sleeps, never gets emotional, never forgets, and can hold a thousand times more information in its working memory than I can. Whoever builds it will not need to sell it. They will need to ration it.”

The Always-On World Model

The PM is not trying to move the market.
The PM is trying to read the market better than anyone else.

RecWM is the sonar, the mission control, the ICU monitor,
the pit wall, and the OODA loop — for the financial system.

Always watching. Always understanding. Always adapting.

The fund that has it will never go back.
The fund that doesn’t will wonder why they keep losing.

💼 Deep Research Perspective

The Weight of the Book

What it actually feels like to manage $800M, and what would make a veteran PM stop losing sleep.

What It Actually Feels Like to Manage $800 Million, and What Would Make Me Stop Losing Sleep

Written from the perspective of a macro PM with 25 years across Soros Fund Management, Brevan Howard, and now running an $800M independent fund.

I. The Thing Nobody Tells You About This Job

There is a number in my head at all times. Right now it is negative fourteen million dollars. That is how much I am down on my Turkish lira short this week. I know this number the way you know your own name. It is there when I wake up, when I eat dinner with my kids, when I am supposedly watching a movie with my wife on a Saturday night. It is there when I brush my teeth. It sits behind every conversation I have with every human being in my life like a subtitle track that never turns off.

People outside this business think portfolio management is about being smart. It is not. It is about being able to carry weight. The weight of the book. The weight of knowing that while you sleep, someone in Tokyo or Sydney or Frankfurt is doing something that could make your quarter or blow up your year. The weight of knowing that your LPs — the pension funds, the endowments, the family offices — are counting on you to not be an idiot, and that being an idiot is something that can happen to you at 3:17am on a Tuesday because a deputy governor of the People's Bank of China said something slightly different from what everyone expected about the lending facility rate.

Let me be specific about the anxiety because people romanticize this job.

The 3am phone check. My phone is always on the nightstand. Always. Face down so the screen light does not wake my wife, but close enough that I can reach it without fully waking up. I have trained myself to do a half-conscious check — roll over, tap the screen, squint at S&P futures, squint at dollar-yen, squint at the 10-year. If the numbers are where I expect, I roll back over and I am asleep again in thirty seconds. If something has moved — if the Nikkei is down 2% or if the euro has spiked 80 pips — then I am awake. Fully, completely, horribly awake. And I will not sleep again until I understand why.

This happens three to four nights a week. My wife has stopped asking what I am doing. She knows.

The Sunday night futures open. Sunday at 6pm Eastern is when the CME opens and S&P futures start trading. Every Sunday, no matter what I am doing, I check. I check at a family barbecue. I checked at my daughter's college move-in day. I checked at a funeral. The Sunday open is a referendum on what happened over the weekend — did anything break? Did some geopolitical event I had not thought about suddenly become the only thing that matters? The Sunday open has ruined more Sunday evenings than I can count. Not because the market always moves — usually it does not. But because there is that seven-second window between tapping my phone and seeing the number where my stomach is in free fall.

Vacations. I have not had a real vacation in twenty years. I have had trips where I bring my laptop and my Bloomberg terminal app and I pretend to be on vacation while checking my book every forty-five minutes. I went to Tuscany with my family three years ago. Beautiful villa, incredible food, stunning countryside. I spent the entire time on the terrace with my phone because the ECB was in the middle of a rate decision cycle and my European rates position was large. My wife took photos. In every single one, I am looking at my phone or my face is lit by a screen. She showed them to me later as an accusation. She was right.

The wedding. A close friend's daughter's wedding, 2019. I had a large long position in Brazilian real, and Bolsonaro's government was making noise about pension reform potentially stalling. I stepped out of the ceremony — the actual ceremony — to check my phone. I told my wife I was going to the bathroom. I stood in the hallway of the church reading a Reuters wire about Rodrigo Maia's comments on the pension vote timeline. I missed the vows. My friend has never mentioned it. I think about it all the time.

This is not a complaint. I chose this. I love this. But I want to be honest about what it costs, because the cost is directly related to what I need.

II. How I Actually Read the World

I do not use models. I have quants on my team who use models, and I listen to them the way I listen to a weather forecast — useful background, but I am looking out the window. My job is synthesis. My job is to take fifty weak signals from fifty different domains and stitch them together into a feeling — a directional conviction about the state of the world — that I can then express through positions.

Here is what this actually looks like on a random Wednesday morning.

5:15am. I wake up and check overnight price action. Not just my positions — everything. Dollar-yen. Aussie-dollar. Copper. Iron ore. The Hang Seng. European bank stocks. Credit spreads in investment grade and high yield. Treasury futures. Bund futures. I am not looking at each number individually. I am looking at the pattern. When copper is down and the Aussie is down and iron ore is down but the Hang Seng is flat, that tells me something different than if all four are down together. The divergences are the information. The things that should be moving together but are not — those are where the signal lives.

5:45am. Bloomberg. I read the TOP headlines but I am mostly scanning for things that do not belong. The headline that seems small but shouldn't be. Three weeks before the SVB collapse, there was a small story about a midsize bank in California seeing deposit outflows. It was buried. Nobody cared. But if you had been tracking the duration mismatch in regional bank portfolios — which I had been, loosely, because a friend at a family office had mentioned it at a dinner — that headline was a five-alarm fire. Most people did not see it. I almost did not see it. I saw it because I was looking for it without knowing I was looking for it. That is what 25 years of pattern recognition does. It makes you a tuning fork for anomaly.

6:30am. Phone calls. I talk to three or four people every morning before the US open. A macro strategist at a bank who is smart. A PM at another fund who runs a different strategy but sees the same markets. My prime broker contact. And usually someone specific to whatever I am most focused on — if I am trading EM, I call my EM guy in London; if I am in rates, I call a rates trader at one of the dealers.

These calls are not about getting "information" in the way people think. I am not getting tips. I am reading tone. When my prime broker calls me to "check in on my margin" unprompted, that is not a check-in. That is him telling me that other clients are getting margin calls, that his risk desk is nervous, that the market is about to go through a de-leveraging event. He cannot say that explicitly. But I have known him for fifteen years and I know what his voice sounds like when he is nervous. That is information. That is alpha.

When the macro strategist at the bank sounds bored, that tells me consensus is settled and there is no energy for a move. When he sounds excited, it means something is about to break out of a range. When he disagrees with me too quickly, it means I am consensus and I should be worried about my position.

7:00am-9:30am. I am reading, thinking, and adjusting my mental model of the world. I read the FT, the WSJ, a few research notes, Twitter (specific accounts I follow who are actually useful — @EpsPlotter, a few anonymous accounts who are clearly on institutional trading desks). I am not reading for facts. I am reading for narrative shifts. Markets do not move on facts. They move on narratives that change. The fact that US employment is strong has been true for two years. It is priced in. What matters is the moment the narrative shifts from "employment is strong" to "employment is too strong and the Fed has to do something about it." That shift does not happen because of a single data point. It happens because a critical mass of people start talking differently. I am trying to detect that shift before it is complete.

9:30am. The open. I watch the first thirty minutes like a hawk. The first thirty minutes of trading tell you more about the real state of supply and demand than any research report ever written. Is there real selling or is it just noise? Are the moves happening on volume or in a vacuum? Where are the big prints? If I see a large block trade in an ETF that tracks emerging market bonds, I want to know who is selling. I cannot always know. But sometimes the pattern of the trade tells you — if it is being worked carefully in small pieces, it is a real account reducing risk. If it is being dumped in a single print, someone just hit a stop-loss or got a redemption.

This is what I do. All day. Every day. I stitch together weak signals from order flow, from conversations, from headlines, from price action, from body language on CNBC, from the fact that three different people mentioned the same obscure thing in the same week. I build a mosaic in my head. And then I express that mosaic as a portfolio.

The problem is that this mosaic lives entirely in my head. It is not written down. It is not systematic. It is not verifiable. I cannot tell you exactly why I think the dollar is about to weaken. I can give you seven reasons, but the real reason is that the pattern feels like 2017 to me, and in 2017 the dollar rolled over after everyone was sure it would keep going. That is not an argument I can put in a research note. That is 25 years of scar tissue talking.

III. What I Wish Existed
