12. Connection to the RCE Formal Core

ADS is not a bolt-on — it is a natural expression of the RCE framework:

Reflexivity. The defense system IS the model's reflexive awareness of its own market impact. Kself, the self-influence kernel, is the formal expression of "the model observing its own effect on the world."
Constructive economics. The adversarial equilibrium IS a constructed reality. The defense strategy does not exist in nature — it is constructed by the model through self-play, and it constructs the market reality in which the model operates by changing the information available to adversaries.
Active inference. The defense system minimizes surprise — specifically, the surprise an adversary can achieve by detecting the model's strategy. The model's niche (the market) infers the model, and the defense system manages what the niche can infer.
DPO + COT. The set of surviving strategies (defended, alpha-generating, unexploitable) forms a chemical organization in strategy space — a self-maintaining set that persists because it is closed under the adversarial dynamics. Strategy retirement, when a signal is compromised, is the death of a species in the strategy ecology. Strategy generation of new alpha sources is speciation.

ADS is where the theory meets the threat. It is the immune system of the trading organism.

Prior Art & What's New

ApproachWhat it doesWhat ADS adds
Almgren-Chriss optimal executionMinimizes impact cost + timing riskAdds an explicit mutual-information leakage penalty; optimal trajectory becomes a martingale in cumulative quantity, not a deterministic schedule
TCA / execution algos (VWAP, POV, IS)Minimize slippage against a benchmarkSelected stochastically as part of a defensibility-calibrated mixed strategy (softmax over near-optimal actions), not chosen deterministically per order
Position-limit / crowding heuristicsStatic caps on concentrated positionsA self-influence kernel (Kself) that detects the model creating its own crowding via price feedback, plus real-time MIS/ADV/flow-correlation external crowding detection with an automatic response matrix
Red-teaming / adversarial ML (general)Static robustness testing before deploymentContinuous, co-evolving three-agent Red Team integrated into live trading on a daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly cadence, with a formal Nash-equilibrium target and a growing agent population
Information-based trading models (Kyle 1985, Glosten-Milgrom)Model how informed trading reveals information to the market via price impactInverts the model into a live control system that actively minimizes revealed information subject to an alpha budget, with an explicit decoy-order and venue-routing mechanism to engineer the inversion
Von Neumann minimax / game-theoretic mixed strategiesEstablishes that mixed strategies are optimal against adaptive adversaries in repeated gamesOperationalizes the abstract result into a calibrated softmax over concrete trading decisions (size, timing, instrument, algo, exit, hedge ratio), each with a measured alpha cost
Known Gaps & Limitations

The Information-Alpha Tradeoff theorem (§1.1) is stated informally and has not been rigorously derived for realistic market microstructure — a design principle backed by intuition and partial analysis, not a peer-reviewed result. The Observational Learning Bound's numeric example (0.02 bits/day, two-year secrecy half-life, §8) rests on stylized assumptions about decoy independence and adversary rationality that will not hold against a Class B adversary with identity-linked position data — the bound as stated assumes the adversary sees only the public tape, explicitly excluding prime-broker-level information. Self-play only defends against the Red Team agents actually built; a materially more capable real-world adversary (Failure Mode 4, §10.2) may exploit vectors the simulation never modeled, with no guarantee the co-evolutionary population converges to a global rather than local equilibrium. The system cannot address catastrophic human information leaks, convergent independent discovery of the same alpha source, or regulatory position-disclosure requirements (13F/13D) — named explicitly as out-of-scope failure modes, not edge cases the architecture happens to miss. The 95–210 bps/year defense-tax estimate and three-year cumulative-alpha comparison (§9) are illustrative projections from the design document, not backtested results. The decoy-generation protocol assumes decoys can be constructed with genuinely near-zero expected P&L and full hedge-out within 24 hours — in practice dependent on the availability of correlated, liquid instruments, not guaranteed for every strategy or asset class.

REN Invention 10-11 · August 2026

Live Architecture & Information Fusion

A three-screen, always-on interface that fuses hundreds of heterogeneous data streams into a single continuously-evolving perceptual field — and automatically restructures itself, in real time, from ambient monitor to crisis action engine.

Overview: Two Inventions, One System

Invention 10 (Live Architecture) is the always-on operating structure: three screens tuned to different attention timescales, a mode machine that transitions between Normal, Elevated, and Crisis states as portfolio health changes, and a progressive-disclosure model that lets a PM extract a decision in half a second or interrogate a causal chain for five minutes, using the same underlying data. Invention 11 (Information Fusion) is what feeds that architecture: the compression of hundreds of simultaneous data streams — price feeds, positioning data, macro fragments, participant models — into a small vocabulary of preattentive visual and audio channels (color, size, motion, texture, sound, haptics) that the human perceptual system can process continuously, below the level of conscious reading.

Design philosophy: Extended Cognition (Clark & Chalmers, 1998). The target is not a dashboard the PM checks — it is an instrument the PM thinks with, the way a blind person's cane extends perception rather than reporting on it. The design brief's own framing: RecWM must reach the point where the PM does not experience it as a separate object. They do not "check RecWM." They do not "look at RecWM." They see the world, and RecWM is how they see it — the cane is not where perception ends, it is where perception begins.

Reading guide. Part A (§1–4) documents the Live Architecture: the three physical screens, the progressive-disclosure resolution ladder, the automatic Normal/Elevated/Crisis mode machine, and the continuous-operation ritual that wraps the trading day. Part B (§5–9) documents Information Fusion: the preattentive visual grammar, the composite metaphors that fuse multiple channels into a single gestalt, the multi-modal (audio/haptic) extension, the social/organizational fusion layer, and the linguistic compression layer. §10 formalizes both as an information-channel problem. §11–15 walk the full mastery-progression and bonding-moment design, which is the behavioral evidence that the architecture achieves cognitive extension rather than remaining a dashboard.

Part A · Live Architecture

1. The Triad of Awareness

Three screens map to three decision timescales, mirroring an F1 pit wall: telemetry (ambient), timing strategy (intermittent focal), team-principal dashboard (on-demand deep dive). The organizing principle is that the same underlying fragment network is rendered three times, at three different information densities and three different physical distances from the PM's body — peripheral vision, arm's length, pulled forward on demand — rather than three different systems bolted together.

ScreenAttention modeContent
Primary · World CanvasPeripheral, preattentiveTopological field: portfolio center, concentric rings of positions → macro fragments → exogenous forces
Secondary · Portfolio ConsoleIntermittent focal (arm's length)Four quadrants: Position Matrix, Fragment Composition, Scenario Tree, Action Queue
Tertiary · Deep Dive TheaterOn-demand, pulled forwardFragment anatomy, scenario counterfactuals, participant theory-of-mind models

1.1 Primary Screen: The World Canvas

The primary screen is a single, continuous, slowly-evolving visual field — the equivalent of a sonar waterfall. No tables. No numbers in the default state. Layout is a large circular topology, radar-display-crossed-with-gravitational-field-map: the portfolio sits at the center; concentric rings radiate outward by proximity of influence — innermost ring holds positions and their direct drivers, middle ring holds macro fragments (rates, credit, volatility regimes), outer ring holds exogenous forces (geopolitical, regulatory, structural). Each fragment is a softly glowing node whose visual properties encode state (full channel grammar in §5).

The Waterfall Strip. Along the bottom of the primary screen runs a horizontal time-series strip — the direct descendant of the submarine sonar waterfall. It shows the last 24 hours of world-canvas state compressed into a scrolling band; each vertical slice is a snapshot of the topology at that moment, rendered as a color column. The PM sees at a glance whether the world has been stable (uniform color bands) or turbulent (jagged, shifting patterns). This strip becomes the PM's time-sense for the market — an intuitive feel for the rhythm of the day develops the same way a sonar operator develops a feel for a patrol.

The Heartbeat Line. A single waveform runs across the top of the primary screen: portfolio health score as a continuous trace, rendered like an ECG. The PM's eye catches the shape of the line — steady and rhythmic in normal conditions, erratic during stress — without reading a single number. This is the ICU-monitor principle: the waveform is the patient, not a report about the patient.

1.2 Secondary Screen: The Portfolio Console

Structured like a Bloomberg terminal reimagined for the world-model era, organized into four quadrants:

QuadrantContentSA level served
Top-left · Position MatrixEvery position, color-coded P&L, 5-day sparkline, plus a RecWM health dot per position reflecting the health of the fragments that drive it — "up 2% and the fragments supporting it are deteriorating"Level 2 (comprehension, not just perception)
Top-right · Fragment Composition PanelActive causal narratives as cards: name (e.g. "Fed Pivot Thesis," "China Credit Stress," "Energy Dislocation"), current probability, trajectory arrow, portfolio impact estimate; sorted by absolute impact"What stories is the world telling me, and which matter for my book?"
Bottom-left · Scenario TreeBranching diagram; trunk = current state; branch thickness = probability; branch color = impact (blue favorable, copper adverse). A narrow blue tree means stay the course; a wide mixed tree means hedge or reduceSpatial read of the shape of the future
Bottom-right · Action QueueRecommended actions ranked by urgency × impact; each card shows what, why (linked to a composition), expected impact, confidence; color-coded blue (opportunity) / amber (risk mgmt) / coral (urgent defense)Bridge from perception to action

1.3 Tertiary Screen: The Deep Dive Theater

A flexible workspace that reconfigures based on what the PM is investigating. Default state: blank dark surface with a subtle logo — an invitation, not a demand. Three populated modes:

Deep-dive modeTriggerContent
Fragment Deep DiveFragment selectedData sources feeding it, historical trajectory with annotated regime changes, causal links to other fragments, confidence decomposition (well-supported vs. inferred), counterfactual analysis ("if this fragment were in state X instead of Y, portfolio impact would be Z")
Scenario Deep DiveScenario branch selectedFull narrative — the chain of events leading to this future, key decision points, historical analogues, specific portfolio impact; scenarios toggle side-by-side
Participant Model ViewMarket participant selected (e.g. "Federal Reserve," "China PBOC," "Systematic Vol Sellers")RecWM's theory-of-mind model of that participant: inferred objectives, constraints, likely actions under different conditions, historical behavior patterns — the market seen through the eyes of its other players

2. Progressive Disclosure

The same underlying fragment network is exposed at four resolutions, each matched to a different decision the PM needs to make. Let S(t) denote the full fragment-network state at time t, and Rk a rendering (projection) operator for disclosure level k ∈ {0,1,2,3}. Each level is a strict information-reducing projection of the level below it:

R0(S) ⊂ R1(S) ⊂ R2(S) ⊂ R3(S) = S

Level 0–1 use only preattentive channels (no reading required); Level 2–3 require focal, sequential reading. Time budget per level: 0.5s, 5s, 30s, 5min — a roughly geometric progression in both time and information content, so the PM's marginal cost of "looking closer" is predictable.

LevelTimeWhat the PM extractsCognitive mode
0 · The Glance0.5sHeartbeat-line shape (steady/erratic/trending); canvas color (predominantly blue = calm, mixed = watchful, amber-coral = stress); canvas geometry (expanded = normal, contracted = correlated stress); any pulsing element demanding "look at me"Zero cognitive load, preattentive only. PM returns to prior conversation knowing "fine" or "look closer soon."
1 · The Scan5sTop-3 fragment compositions by portfolio impact (names + trajectory arrows only); coral action items; scenario-tree shape (narrow=predictable vs. branching=uncertain); position P&L heatmapFocal attention, minimal reading. Answers "what is the state of the world and my portfolio right now?"
2 · The Read30sComposition probability estimates and evidence summaries; one-sentence scenario narratives; action-queue rationale; per-position risk decomposition by driving fragmentActive reading and analysis. Answers "what should I be thinking about, and what might I need to do?"
3 · The Deep Dive5minFull fragment anatomy (sources, history, confidence bounds); scenario counterfactuals ("what if X doesn't happen, what if Y happens instead"); participant-model interrogation; historical-analogue comparison ("when has the world looked like this before, and what happened next"); portfolio simulation against a proposed tradeThe deep work — RecWM as a full analytical partner, not a display

This four-level ladder is a direct product-level instantiation of Endsley's three-level Situational Awareness model (perception → comprehension → projection): Levels 0–1 are perception, Level 2 is comprehension, Level 3 is projection. The novelty is not the SA taxonomy itself (that is 1980s human-factors research) but making it a literal, navigable UI ladder over a live causal fragment network rather than a static cockpit instrument panel.

3. The Mode Machine: Normal → Elevated → Crisis

The interface is not static — it automatically transforms based on aggregate fragment-network health, moving from a perception engine to an action engine as urgency rises. This is a genuine finite-state machine driven by a scalar health signal, not a manual view toggle.

Let h(t) ∈ [1,10] be the portfolio health score at time t, and M(t) ∈ {Normal, Elevated, Crisis} the interface mode. The transition function is a threshold map with hysteresis on the recovery boundary (crisis exit requires h > 6, not merely ≥ 4, to avoid mode-flapping at the boundary):

M(t) = Normal  if h(t) ≥ 7
M(t) = Elevated  if 4 ≤ h(t) < 7
M(t) = Crisis  if h(t) < 4, exits only once h(t) > 6
ModeHealthLayout change
Normal7–10Full ambient display, standard density, exploratory tools available. The PM browses, explores, thinks.
Elevated4–6World canvas subtly intensifies; background darkens slightly; heartbeat line becomes more prominent; Action Queue promoted from bottom-right to top-right quadrant, displacing Fragment Composition (pushed to tertiary screen). Message: "Pay attention. You may need to act."
Crisis1–3World canvas contracts sharply — fragments pull together, connections blaze bright, peripheral edge-glow flares. Four quadrants collapse to two panels; communication bar appears; tertiary screen becomes a full-screen war-room simulator

Crisis-mode left panel: The Situation Board. A real-time, auto-updating narrative, not raw data feeds — continuously generated human-readable account: "Credit stress has cascaded from Asia HY into European IG. Dealer liquidity indicators suggest market-making capacity has dropped 40% from yesterday. The Fed Pivot scenario has been pruned — the model now assigns 85% probability to a Liquidity Vortex composition. Portfolio health is 2 and declining."

Crisis-mode right panel: The Action Board. Pre-computed playbooks activated as one-click execution packages: "Playbook: Defensive De-risk. Actions: Reduce HY exposure by 30%, add 3M put spread on HYG, increase cash to 15%. Estimated cost: 45bp of carry. Estimated health improvement: from 2 to 5. Execute?"

A communication bar sits atop the secondary screen with one-click buttons — "Alert CIO," "Alert Risk Team," "Alert Traders" — each pre-loaded with a context-appropriate message generated from RecWM's situational assessment. The tertiary screen becomes the war room: a full-screen scenario-simulation environment for real-time stress-testing of a proposed response ("if I execute the defensive playbook AND the Vortex deepens, where do I end up?").

The Debrief. After crisis mode ends (health recovers above 6), RecWM automatically generates a structured Crisis Debrief: timeline of events and fragment-state transitions; actions taken (both RecWM recommendations and PM decisions); portfolio impact analysis (what was lost, what was saved by defensive action); model performance assessment (what RecWM predicted correctly vs. missed); lessons folded into future playbooks. The debrief is a dual-purpose learning artifact — for the PM and for RecWM's own model improvement loop.

FUNCTION mode_machine(h_t, mode_prev): IF mode_prev == CRISIS: IF h_t > 6: RETURN NORMAL_OR_ELEVATED(h_t) // hysteresis: exit only above 6 ELSE: RETURN CRISIS ELSE: IF h_t < 4: RETURN CRISIS ELSE IF h_t < 7: RETURN ELEVATED ELSE: RETURN NORMAL FUNCTION render(mode, S_t): IF mode == NORMAL: layout = FOUR_QUADRANT(Position, Composition, Scenario, Action) IF mode == ELEVATED: layout = FOUR_QUADRANT(Position, Action, Scenario, Composition_to_tertiary) IF mode == CRISIS: layout = TWO_PANEL(SituationBoard(S_t), ActionBoard(playbooks(S_t))) tertiary = WAR_ROOM_SIM(S_t) RETURN layout

4. Continuous Operation: The Morning Ritual

Live Architecture means the system never fully stops running — it compresses and re-expands around the PM's attention cycle rather than presenting a cold-start dashboard each session. Design principle: Sacred Augmentation — the existing PM ritual (wake, check phone, Bloomberg scan, morning meeting, position review) is not replaced but layered onto, so that within three months the PM cannot remember what the ritual felt like before RecWM.

PhaseTimeMechanism
Pre-Dawn Push6:00 AMSingle haptic pulse (not an alarm, not a notification). Lock-screen widget shows: (1) the Health Number, a single 1–10 integer, color-coded — 7+ and the PM relaxes, below 5 and they reach for the phone; (2) the Headline Fragment, one editorial sentence — "Credit stress in Asia-Pacific intensified; HY spread fragment shifted from blue to amber"; (3) the Delta Count — "3 fragments shifted" tells the PM whether the world moved or held still overnight. Total absorption time: 3 seconds.
Commute Brief6:30–7:30 AMOn tablet or landscape phone: a structured, scrollable Morning Brief — the Bloomberg FIRST function rebuilt for the world-model era. Five components: (1) Overnight Narrative, ~200 words, told as coherent story not a data list; (2) Fragment State Changes, tabular before/after with driver and portfolio relevance; (3) Scenario Tree Update — which branches grew, shrank, emerged, or were pruned; (4) Today's Watch List — explicit trigger thresholds, e.g. "if 10Y breaks 4.50%, the rate regime fragment transitions to 'restrictive,' triggering a cascade into equity risk premium and credit spread fragments"; (5) Recommended Pre-Open Actions with rationale and urgency
Console Activation7:30 AMScreens wake; world canvas populates with a 3-second assembly animation (fragments appearing and connecting, the topology assembling like a living organism) — deliberately non-informational, a ritual element. The secondary screen then shows, for exactly 30 seconds, a "Delta View" — a focused summary of everything that changed since the PM last looked — before reverting to the standard four-quadrant layout (or on the PM's first click, whichever comes first).

Continuity itself is a designed feature: when the console goes offline for scheduled maintenance, it generates a reconnection brief on restart — "During the 36 hours offline, 7 fragments shifted state. Two compositions were activated that would have triggered amber alerts. Summary of missed signals follows." — making the coverage gap explicit rather than silent, which is itself an engineered dependency mechanism (see §13, Moment 4).

Sample Overnight Narrative text from the design brief, illustrating the required narrative (not bulleted) register: "Asian credit markets showed continued stress overnight, driven by property developer liquidity concerns that have now propagated into the broader HY complex. The Liquidity Stress fragment moved from 4.2 to 5.8, crossing the amber threshold. European open reflected this with a 15bp widening in iTraxx crossover. The rate trajectory fragment remained stable, suggesting this is isolated credit stress rather than a broader risk-off event."

Part B · Information Fusion

5. Preattentive Encoding as a Fusion Channel

The core fusion problem: hundreds of simultaneous data streams (price feeds, positioning data, macro regime indicators, news, participant behavior models) must be compressed into a form a human can monitor continuously without reading. The design draws on Healey & Enns (2012): color, orientation, size, motion, shape, and spatial grouping can be detected in under 200ms without focused attention — the visual system's preattentive processing stage, which operates in parallel across the whole visual field rather than serially like reading. Every fragment node in the World Canvas encodes state through exactly these channels, and only these channels, in the default (Level 0/1) state:

Visual channelEncodesMechanism
ColorHealth stateContinuous gradient deep blue → teal → amber → coral (never a discrete traffic light, because markets don't jump from green to red — the palette must support the same continuity as the underlying process)
SizeMagnitude of portfolio relevanceNodes physically expand as influence grows over the trailing 48h; a fragment growing in importance is visible without reading a number
MotionRate of changeStill (stable) → gentle wobble like a gyroscope losing its axis (transitioning) → slow rhythmic pulse, expansion/contraction like breathing (rapid transition); targets peripheral motion detection in visual cortex area MT/V5, which operates below conscious awareness — the PM feels movement before knowing what moved
ConnectionsCorrelation strength and signLine opacity = strength; blue = positive coupling, muted copper = negative; thicken and brighten during regime transitions, visually showing the system's coupling tighten in real time
TextureConfidence / uncertaintySharp, clean edges = high confidence; soft, slightly grainy "frosted glass" boundary = low confidence — the PM learns to distrust the fuzzy ones without being told to

Treating each preattentive channel as an independent, low-bandwidth information channel makes the design constraint explicit. If a channel supports ni reliably-discriminable states under a <200ms exposure, its preattentive channel capacity is approximately

Ci ≈ log2(ni) bits

Color on a 4-stop continuous gradient (blue/teal/amber/coral) carries roughly 2 bits reliably at a glance; size (3–4 discriminable magnitudes) another ~2 bits; motion state (still/wobble/pulse) ~1.6 bits; texture (sharp/frosted, effectively binary under peripheral viewing) ~1 bit. The five-channel World Canvas node therefore fuses on the order of 6–8 bits of state per fragment into a single preattentive glance — enough to distinguish roughly 60–250 joint states per node without a single number being read. This is the quantitative version of the design claim "no numbers in the default state": the bit budget of the ambient channel set must exceed the bit budget the PM actually needs at Level 0/1, or the design collapses back into a table.

5.1 Composite Metaphors: Fusing Multiple Channels into One Gestalt

The five channels above are combined into whole-canvas composite metaphors, each mapped to a specific abstract market state that would otherwise require reading a matrix or a multi-series chart:

Market stateComposite renderingPerceptual mechanism invoked
Liquidity StressCanvas literally contracts — nodes pull closer together, connection lines thicken and brighten, background shifts from dark charcoal toward a deep bruised purple as stress deepensGravitational-collapse metaphor; same instinct as a school of fish tightening into a ball when a predator approaches
Regime TransitionWhole-display texture changes: a subtle shimmer, low-frequency oscillation across all elements, like heat haze over a highway, intensifying as transition probability risesTriggers a pre-verbal "something is different" response before the PM can articulate what changed
Momentum ShiftA reversing fragment's node develops rotation — slowly spins, decelerates, stops, reverses direction, like a wheel changing directionMotion-detection circuits pick up the deceleration before the reversal completes — preconscious lead time
Consensus DivergenceWhen participant models begin to disagree (a crowded trade fragmenting), relevant nodes flicker — alternating between two colors at a rate just below the flicker-fusion thresholdVisual dissonance: the PM feels instability without knowing why
Tail Risk AccumulationThe outer ring, which normally fades to darkness at its edge, begins to glow faintly — a dim warm light at the periphery, like dawn on the horizonExploits hardwired sensitivity to peripheral-field change (evolutionary predator-detection adaptation) — registers "something building at the edges" before any formal alert fires

6. Multi-Modal Fusion: Sound and Haptics

Fusion is not limited to vision. An optional ambient audio layer (a PM preference setting, per Hermann et al. 2011 auditory-display research) sonifies market state as a continuous, low-volume texture processed in parallel with visual attention and conversation — the sonar operator's headphones, not an alarm and not speech.

Market conditionSonic rendering
NormalLow, steady hum, barely audible, like a distant machine
Rising volatilityPitch rises slightly, texture becomes more granular
StressA subtle rhythmic pulse emerges
CrisisFrequency spectrum widens into a broader, more complex sound

Reference model: film-sound "room tone" — the barely perceptible ambience that tells you whether you are in a cathedral or a submarine without a single line of dialogue. Required properties: non-fatiguing over 10+ hours of continuous exposure; distinguishable from office background noise; emotionally neutral at baseline; capable of conveying urgency without triggering a startle response; processable by the auditory cortex in parallel with speech, so the PM can hold a conversation while still monitoring.

Mobile haptics extend the same fused-signal principle to a third modality via the Taptic Engine (or equivalent):

Haptic patternMeaning
Single pulseInformational notification (morning brief is ready)
Double pulseAttention requested (fragment crossed threshold)
Continuous vibration (200ms)Action required (crisis mode activated)

The PM's phone becomes a peripheral awareness device — they feel the market through their pocket, extending the fusion architecture beyond the desk entirely.

7. Fusion Across People: The Social Layer

The same fusion architecture operates at the organizational level, transforming individual cognitive extension into collective intelligence.

The CIO View. The CIO does not need individual fragments — they need aggregate team health, rendered as a single screen: a PM Health Grid (each PM's portfolio health score as a color-coded matrix, so the CIO sees at a glance who is in good shape and who is under stress); a Correlation Map (how correlated are the PM portfolios — are they all exposed to the same fragments, revealing crowding risk across the team); a Scenario Impact Matrix (under each major scenario branch, what happens to total fund exposure — "if the Liquidity Vortex scenario materializes, PM A and PM C are both heavily impacted, but PM B is naturally hedged"); and Aggregate Fragment Health, the fund-level world canvas showing which fragments matter most for the fund as a whole.

PM-to-PM Communication. Two PMs can "share canvases" — overlaying their individual fragment views to see where perceptions agree and diverge: "My credit fragment is amber, yours is still teal — what are you seeing that I'm not?" This is a richer, more structured form of the hallway conversation. Mechanically: a "Share View" button on any fragment or composition opens a lightweight communication panel; the PM sends a fragment state to a colleague with a one-line annotation; the recipient sees it overlaid on their own canvas. This is not messaging — it is shared perception, a direct fusion of two independently-computed but structurally comparable world-model views.

The Morning Meeting Transformation. RecWM turns the morning meeting from a sequential briefing ("PM A reports, PM B reports…") into collaborative situational assessment. The meeting-room screen shows the aggregate world canvas; PMs add their own overlays; the CIO sees the synthesized picture. Illustrative exchange from the design brief: CIO asks "Who is below 7?" — two PMs raise hands. "What fragments?" — "Credit for me, rates for me." "Are they connected?" — RecWM shows the correlation: yes, both driven by the Liquidity Stress composition. Three minutes to surface a concentrated risk that would have taken thirty minutes of discussion in the old format.

8. Shared Language as a Fusion Compression Layer

Fusion also happens linguistically — a shared vocabulary is itself a lossy-but-efficient compression code for a rich underlying state, the same role "pull up a GP" plays for a Bloomberg user.

Lexical categoryVocabularyWhat it compresses
Fragment state (color)"Deep blue" / "Teal" / "Amber" / "Coral"Stable-favorable / neutral-watchful / stressed-transitioning / critical-active-deterioration — "the credit fragment went amber overnight" fuses state, trajectory, urgency and domain into four words
Health score (numeric)9–10 "Strong" · 7–8 "Sound" · 5–6 "Watchful" · 3–4 "Stressed" · 1–2 "Critical""We are running at a 6 with credit pulling us down" becomes the opening line of the morning meeting
Composition names"Liquidity Vortex" (multiple liquidity indicators converging into self-reinforcing stress) · "Rate Regime Pivot" (fundamental shift in rate expectations) · "Correlation Storm" (cross-asset correlations spiking simultaneously) · "The Unwind" (a crowded position reversing) · "Slow Burn" (a risk accumulating gradually below threshold with persistent trajectory)"Are we in a Slow Burn?" replaces "Is there a gradually building risk that hasn't triggered any alerts yet?"
Scenario shorthand"We are on the March-2020 branch" · "We are on the 2013-Taper-Tantrum branch"Historical-analogue labels instantly communicate a whole regime-shape (rapid/correlated/liquidity-driven vs. rate-driven/disorderly-but-contained) in one sentence
Tribal markers"What color is your book?" · "The canvas is contracting" · "I've got shimmer on the rates fragment" · "We need to prune the tree"Fragment health (not P&L) · correlation stress building · regime transition detected · reduce scenario count through decisive action — each marks the speaker as a RecWM user, the way jargon marks any professional tribe
Why This Matters for Trading

Speed of correct reaction. A PM glancing up from an unrelated conversation absorbs "the canvas is contracting" (correlation stress building) in half a second via peripheral motion detection — well before a Bloomberg-style scan of a correlation matrix would register the same fact. In a fast liquidity event, that half-second-to-5-second lead is the difference between hedging pre-selloff and hedging into it.

Fusion catches what single-stream monitoring misses. The "It Saw It Before I Did" bonding pattern in the source design is concrete: a subtle shift in dealer positioning data combined with an unusual options-flow pattern — individually sub-threshold on any single feed — becomes visible only when fused into one fragment-network signal. The documented example: flagged Tuesday, hedged Wednesday morning, market in full risk-off by Thursday.

Crisis mode compresses decision latency. Instead of a PM manually pulling together a narrative from six terminals during a drawdown, the Situation Board auto-generates it ("dealer liquidity capacity down 40% from yesterday, Fed Pivot scenario pruned, Liquidity Vortex composition now 85% probability") and the Action Board offers a pre-costed, one-click playbook with an estimated health delta. The illustrative Q3 example in the design brief: early detection 4 hours ahead of a selloff, drawdown reduced from an estimated -3.2% to an actual -0.8%, ~$12M of avoided loss attributed directly to the fused early signal.

Organizational crowding detection. Because every PM's fragment exposure is fused into one CIO-level correlation map, the fund can see book-wide concentration risk ("PM A and PM C both heavily impacted under the Liquidity Vortex scenario, PM B naturally hedged") that no individual PM's terminal would surface.

Part C · Mastery Progression, Bonding Design, and Physical Specification

9. The Stradivarius Effect: Mastery Progression

Design principle: a Stradivarius does not sound better than a student violin to a beginner — it reveals its qualities as the player's skill increases. RecWM is designed on the same curve: always immediately useful, but increasingly powerful as the PM develops fluency, with an explicit milestone trigger marking each phase transition.

PhaseSA levelWhat the PM doesWhat RecWM revealsMilestone trigger
Week 1 · Dashboard PhaseLevel 1, PerceptionTreats RecWM as a sophisticated dashboard: checks health score, reads morning brief, looks at position P&LClean, immediately useful information without overwhelm; the world canvas is beautiful but mostly decorative to a new user; compositions shown simply (name, status, impact)PM checks RecWM before Bloomberg for the first time — unforced, happens naturally because the morning brief is more narratively coherent than scanning Bloomberg screens
Month 1 · Comprehension PhaseLevel 2, ComprehensionBegins reading fragment compositions in detail; starts asking "why?", clicking through to tertiary; begins using fragment names in conversationDeeper causal analysis: clicking a fragment reveals upstream drivers — "Credit is amber BECAUSE liquidity stress is building BECAUSE dealer balance sheets are constrained BECAUSE of quarter-end dynamics"PM makes a trade decision influenced by a composition rather than a single data point; says in the morning meeting, "The model is showing a credit stress composition that concerns me"
Month 3 · Projection PhaseLevel 3, ProjectionActively uses the scenario tree for decisions; asks "what if?", runs counterfactuals; begins to feel the canvas rhythm preconsciouslyPredictive compositions: the scenario tree becomes a decision tool, not a display; PM simulates trades against scenarios — "if I add this position, how does my health score change across the top three branches?"PM catches a risk they would not have seen without RecWM — the "it saw it before I did" moment; first deep bonding event
Month 6 · Extension PhaseCognitive extension achievedStops treating RecWM as a separate tool; ritual and vocabulary fully integrated; cannot separate own judgment from RecWM's contribution because there is no separation leftRecWM begins visibly adapting to the PM: morning brief emphasizes what they care about, action queue favors their preferred trade types, scenario tree highlights branches they find relevant — learning the PM's investment personalityRecWM goes down for scheduled Saturday-night maintenance; Monday morning the PM feels blind — reaches for the canvas with their eyes and finds dark screens; lasts 4 hours; relief on reconnection described as "getting my vision back"
Year 1 · Mastery PhasePermanent cognitive alterationMental model of the market permanently restructured: thinks in fragments, compositions and scenarios even away from the terminal; automatically translates news into fragment impacts; evaluates macro arguments against the scenario tree; faster, more precise, more calibrated than a year prior—PM tries a competing product and closes it within 30 minutes — not because it's measurably worse, but because it doesn't think the way they now think. RecWM has become their cognitive dialect; everything else is a foreign language.

10. Engineered Bonding Moments

Design principle: bonding moments cannot be forced, but the architecture can be built to create the conditions for them. Four specific moment-types are designed for explicitly.

10.1 "It Saw It Before I Did"

RecWM's fragment network has a broader perceptual field than any human PM — it monitors hundreds of data streams simultaneously. The early-detection moment fires when RecWM highlights a pattern (e.g. a subtle shift in dealer positioning data combined with an unusual options-flow pattern) the PM had not noticed. Product experience: a fragment shifts blue→teal; the PM investigates, discovers a risk, acts; the risk materializes the next day; the story becomes organizational mythology at the morning meeting — "RecWM flagged the dealer positioning shift on Tuesday. We hedged Wednesday morning. By Thursday, the market was in full risk-off." This narrative, per the design brief, sells RecWM internally better than any presentation.

Calibration constraint (explicit in the source). The early-detection alert must be delivered at the right confidence calibration: too many false positives destroy trust; too few miss the bonding moment. The precision-recall tradeoff is stated qualitatively, favoring rare, high-quality detections over frequent noisy ones — "better to alert 5 times a year and be right 4 times than to alert 50 times and be right 10 times." No quantitative precision/recall target or validation methodology is given in the source; this is a design preference, not a measured operating point.

10.2 "It Saved Me"

The crisis interface is designed specifically to enable this moment: when a PM executes a defensive playbook and the avoided loss becomes quantifiable, RecWM calculates and presents an "avoided loss" figure in the Crisis Debrief. Illustrative product narrative from the source: "During the Q3 liquidity event, RecWM's Liquidity Vortex detection triggered 4 hours before the market selloff. The defensive playbook reduced portfolio drawdown from an estimated -3.2% to an actual -0.8%. Estimated value of early action: $12M." This is framed as the moment that makes RecWM un-cancellable — every future budget conversation is answered with a specific dollar figure.

10.3 "It Knows Me"

RecWM's adaptation layer learns the PM's cognitive style over time, not just their positions: narrative vs. quantitative briefing preference, mean-reversion vs. momentum orientation, early vs. late hedging tendency, gradual vs. decisive position adjustment. After 6 months, the PM notices the morning brief emphasizes exactly what they would ask about, the action queue favors their style of trade, and the scenario tree highlights the branches they find most decision-relevant — an uncanny "gets me" feeling, explicitly distinguished in the source from an artificial chatbot-style personalization: it is framed as resembling a well-trained human assistant anticipating needs, termed "cognitive symbiosis."

10.4 "I Cannot Go Back"

This moment is not separately engineered — it emerges from the previous three — but it is recognized and reinforced structurally. When RecWM detects it has been offline (maintenance or fault), it generates a reconnection brief on restart: "While you were disconnected, here is what happened and what you missed." Product experience: the PM returns Monday morning after a weekend maintenance window and reads — "During the 36 hours offline, 7 fragments shifted state. Two compositions were activated that would have triggered amber alerts. Summary of missed signals follows." The intended PM reaction, per the source: "I was flying blind and didn't even know it." This is described as the moment of permanent dependency.

11. Design Specifications and Perceptual Rationale

11.1 Color System

The palette is deliberate and grounded in color-perception and emotional-association research:

ColorHex rangeRationale
Deep blue#1a3a5c – #2d6ca2Stability, depth, trust; activates the parasympathetic nervous system — calming. Stable market states should feel calming.
Teal#2d8a8a – #4db8a4Watchfulness without alarm; the transition color, signaling "something has changed" without triggering a stress response
Amber#c4873b – #d4a24cAttention, warmth, urgency; the universal caution color, visible in peripheral vision, unambiguous in meaning
Coral#c75c5c – #d44a4aAction, danger, criticality — deliberately not pure red (which triggers panic and narrows attention) but coral, which demands attention while preserving cognitive breadth
Background#0a0e14 – #141a24Always dark — functional, not aesthetic: reduces eye strain over extended viewing, improves color-coded-element visibility, and creates the immersive "cockpit" quality that supports cognitive extension. The PM should feel inside the display, not looking at it.

11.2 Typography

A single typeface family across the system: a custom monospace variant for data (position names, numbers, fragment labels) and a proportional variant for narrative text (morning brief, scenario descriptions). Numbers use tabular figures exclusively so columns align. Rendered at high contrast against the dark background but at a size that discourages reading from across the room — RecWM is a personal cognitive instrument, not a wall display.

11.3 Animation Principles

All animations are continuous and organic — no sudden jumps, no step changes, no blinking. The world canvas evolves like a living organism: nodes drift, connections flex, colors shift gradually. Animation speed is tuned to be fast enough to convey change but slow enough to avoid distraction. Target cycle: 2–4 seconds for any visual transition — matched to the natural rhythm of breathing, creating a meditative quality that supports sustained attention over a trading day.

11.4 Sound Design and Haptics

Covered in full in §6; specified here as a hard design constraint: the ambient audio layer must be designed by a sound designer, not an engineer, and must satisfy non-fatiguing 10+ hour exposure, distinguishability from office noise, baseline emotional neutrality, urgency-without-startle, and parallel processability with speech.

Prior Art & What's New

ApproachWhat it doesWhat Live Architecture / Fusion adds
Bloomberg Terminal / multi-screen trading desksDense, numerical, table-driven display of independent data feedsReplaces tables with a single continuously-evolving topological field encoding state via preattentive channels, not digits
Alert / threshold monitoring systemsDiscrete rule-based alerts when a metric crosses a static thresholdContinuous ambient gradient (color/size/motion) that surfaces drift before any hard threshold is crossed, plus automatic mode transitions rather than a single alert event
ICU-style single-signal dashboards (heart-rate monitors, F1 telemetry walls)One instrument, one waveform, one operatorExtends the same preattentive-waveform principle to a multi-fragment causal network with drill-down, shared across a trading desk
Data sonification research (Hermann et al. 2011)Demonstrates auditory channels can carry monitoring information in parallel with visual attentionOperationalizes it as a production ambient audio layer tied to live fragment-network state, plus a matched haptic vocabulary
Situational-awareness models (Endsley's 3-level SA)Theoretical framework: perception → comprehension → projectionMaps SA levels directly onto the progressive-disclosure UI (Level 0/1 = perception, Level 2 = comprehension, Level 3 = projection) as a concrete product mechanism
Preattentive-processing / visualization research (Healey & Enns 2012)Catalogues which visual features are detectable in <200ms without focused attentionUses the catalogue as an exhaustive encoding budget for a live financial-fragment network, with an explicit channel-capacity argument (§5) for why five channels suffice
Extended-cognition philosophy (Clark & Chalmers 1998)Argues tools can become literal components of cognition (the blind person's cane)Operationalizes the philosophical claim as a measurable product target — a five-phase mastery curve with explicit, observable milestone triggers (§9) rather than a metaphor
Consumer/enterprise dashboards with personalization ("smart" widgets, ML-ranked feeds)Reorders content by predicted relevance using engagement signalsPersonalization target is trading style and risk posture (mean-reversion vs. momentum, early vs. late hedger) inferred from decisions, not click-through — feeding directly into action-queue ranking and morning-brief emphasis
Known Gaps

The source design brief is a product/UX architecture document, not an engineering specification: it does not define the backend continual-learning mechanism that keeps the fragment network updated without catastrophic forgetting, nor the data-fusion pipeline's latency, consistency, or failure-handling guarantees when heterogeneous feeds (price, filings, satellite, news) disagree or arrive out of order. Claimed neuroscience mechanisms (motion detection via area MT/V5, "just-below-fusion-threshold" flicker) are asserted from general perception research, not validated in this specific interface via user testing. The bonding-moment examples ("It Saw It Before I Did," the $12M avoided-loss figure) are illustrative product narratives in the design document, not measured outcomes from a deployed system. Precision/recall calibration for early-detection alerts is specified only as a qualitative preference ("5 alerts a year, right 4 times, beats 50 alerts right 10 times") with no quantitative target or validation methodology. The crisis-mode automatic playbooks assume pre-computed, pre-costed responses exist for the scenario in progress — there is no described fallback for a genuinely novel crisis pattern outside the playbook library. The information-channel-capacity argument in §5 is an original formalization added to make the "no numbers needed" claim quantitatively checkable; it is not in the source brief and its per-channel bit estimates (2 bits color, 2 bits size, 1.6 bits motion, 1 bit texture) are illustrative order-of-magnitude figures, not measured discrimination thresholds from a psychophysics study of this specific interface. The mastery-progression timeline (week 1 / month 1 / month 3 / month 6 / year 1) and its milestone triggers are design targets, not outcomes observed in a fielded pilot.

Conclusion: The Instrument, Not the Tool

The ultimate measure of success for this pair of inventions is not whether PMs "like" the interface or find it "useful." It is whether, after six months of use, the PM's cognitive architecture has been measurably altered — whether they perceive markets differently, think about risk differently, and make decisions differently in ways they cannot fully articulate or reverse. RecWM's Live Architecture and Information Fusion layers are designed, end to end, to be a cognitive prosthetic rather than a dashboard, an analytics platform, or a decision-support tool: an artificial organ of financial perception that, once integrated, becomes indistinguishable from the PM's own intelligence — not a window the PM looks through, but an eye they see with.
